text: I sent this complaint to Pep Boys and will be filing a complaint with the BBB. I removed personal information. Do not go to this place. If you car needs work, please tow it to a more trustworty garage. Dear Sir or Madam: I am writing to you with respect to the Pep Boys location on Aramingo Avenue in Philadelphia, PA. I broke down on June 18, 2011 at a red light right outside of this location. I was fortunate that I could push my vehicle in the parking lot. I explained to the service employees that my car shut down and was not starting. A woman named Stacey explained to me that they would have to perform a diagnostic test to determine what was wrong with the vehicle. A few hours later, I received a phone call from Stacey explaining to me that I had a bad fuel pump inside of my gas tank that would need to be replaced. The price was about $660. I told them to proceed with the repairs and to call me when the vehicle was ready. I was also advised that a fuel pump would need to be ordered from a dealership and shipped to the store; therefore, the repairs would take a couple of days. The car was ready on Thursday; however, I was out of town until Saturday. I picked up the car on Saturday and drove my car 0.6 miles to the place in which I park my car weekly. The next time I started my car was on Monday evening at which time the vehicle shutdown again. I had noticed the vehicle's EGC light had come on when I received the car from. I called the Pep Boy's location Tuesday morning (I had to take the day off of work) and advised that my car is still not fixed as it is shut down. I requested that they tow the car back to their location at their expense to which they replied that I need to call the Pep Boys 800 number. When I called the 800 number, the woman I spoke with advised that waiving the cost of the tow is at the discretion of the store manager. In order to avoid a bureaucratic/time consuming deadlock, I had the vehicle towed at my own expense to the store. I explained the situation to a manager, Rafael Delgado, Manager #12. I told him that I brought the car in to be fixed and that it was not fixed. I had purchased a warranty on the work that was done on the vehicle. Mr. Delgado explained to me that I have an electrical problem and that I would need to pay for another "electrical diagnostic" (as opposed to a "no start diagnostic" )and the subsequent work that would need to be done on the car. I explained my position that the bad fuel pump was not my diagnosis and I brought the car in and paid with the expectation that my car would be fixed regardless of the what was wrong with the vehicle. He told me that all he could do was check that the work that was under warranty was performed correctly. That, however, did not address the fact that they may have misdiagnosed the issue or did not perform the due diligence necessary to make sure that the actual issue was identified and repair. I also told him that the EGC light was on and that it was not on before I took the car to them. He did not have an answer to this inquiry. In addition, after taking a look at the vehicle, Mr. Delgado brought me into the garage where he showed me that a radiator fan had loosened and frayed a tube with wiring and that the wiring was exposed and could be causing the vehicle's computer to shut the car down. He then advised that his garage had limited capability for European vehicles and could not perform the repairs to actually fix the problem. I then asked him why he changed my fuel pump when it was obvious that the issue was the fan and wire. He advised that the car had no fuel pressure according to the diagnostic and repeated that he could not fix the vehicle and that I should tow it to a dealership to have it fixed. I asked him to produce a copy of the original diagnostic report and he could not. I am very disappointed at the lack of professionalism and diligence at this branch. In addition, please see this yelp.com link where a prior customer (Aubrey A.) details almost exactly what I experienced. It is very disappointing to know that your organization is being represented by personnel that I can only assume are either incompetent or purposely misleading customers into having their vehicle's fuel pump replaced. According to the reviews on the internet, this is a very poor performing branch of your company.

That this place bills itself a bed and breakfast is an insult to the word breakfast. I can understand that not every bed and breakfast can make homemade pastries, but if you must buy them from the corner 7-11, at least take them out of the plastic wrapper and put them on a serving tray and pretend that you care. The low quality food and complete lack of class is quite a contrast to the surroundings of the hotel. text: This place is FANTASTIC. I have to be completely honest about my original draw to this restaurant. My mother loves Rocky Balboa, so I took to a Google search to find out where "Adrian's Restaurant" was located in the city. I scoped out the website and saw that it seemed like an inviting, South Philly Italian restaurant. We had been to Ralph's and a few others in the city but nothing really blew us away. We called at about 6PM on a Saturday night, and the two of us were able to get a 7:30 reservation-- not without a quick moment of speculation. So if you're planning on a visit, especially with anymore than two people, call ahead. The place appears very quaint from the typical South Philly street on Dickinson. Once inside, the place was thriving: the wait staff criss-crossed the restaurant, preparing tables and serving the other patrons, a mild-mannered round young man bellowing out some famous aria I couldn't identify, the owners (or management?) were answering a phone that seemingly rang every other minute. Following the performance we were promptly seated and given menus and the specials by are server Jason. If there were one complaint, it would be that the wait staff is apparently responsible for every function of the restaurant outside of the kitchen. You will see these guys clean and prep tables, serve food, sing, get nagged by customers for photos, and I counted no less than four happy birthday promenades, complete with four-part harmony. The food was fantastic. If you're ordering a salad, two can split one-- though I had no problem housing my baby arugula salad by myself. The salad was the best I have ever eaten. Perfectly aged balsamic vinegar, a nice Italian cheese that I cant remember, sliced pears, walnuts- truly a perfect match. The penne dish was tasty, adorned with tender chicken, tomatoes, parsley and mozzarella. I could see where some may be critical of this dish, however I felt it was perfectly balanced and filling. My mother had the scallops and shrimp pasta dish. The scallops were perfectly tender, not at all chewy nor over-cooked. The ambiance of this place is truly what makes it. You can really feel the "living history" the moment you set foot inside. The owners told us of the history of the property, which takes its name from its opening in 1918 as a RCA Victor record store. The place would make a great date to really impress. I plan on bringing my girlfriend to see this place. Upstairs is a cozy bar you can slip away to after your meal. All in all, a great place. I will be back.

text: A friend and I had dinner here on Sunday, November 13, and couldn't have been happier. We didn't have a reservation, but when we called, we were welcomed and told they'd accommodate us when we arrived. That's exactly what happened when we did arrive. We were interested in sharing some dishes to maximize flavor experiences and minimize calories, so we decided on the calamari and rock shrimp with tempura veggies as an appetizer, and then a special entree of the night plus roasted veggies. We came to this decision with the help of our excellent server who clearly wanted us to have a great evening. Wines by the glass are very diverse, and quite reasonable. We each enjoyed a glass to our taste that paired well with the food we had ordered. Now to discuss the food: Calamari-Rock shrimp-tempura vegetables: delicious and perfectly prepared with an amazing variety of veggies (including fennel!); perhaps a bit more seafood would have been nice, but we were happy. Entree: this special was a trio of seafoods: grilled salmon with a polenta cake, sea bass with mushroom risotto, and fried trout with a bit of salad. We split each of these, and still had plenty of food, and each of the trio tasted excellent (tiny quibbles: the salmon could have been cooked a bit less, and everything needed some salt and pepper). Grilled vegetables: asparagus, portabellas, carrots, squash, fennel, green beans and more were on this platter. They were the perfect accompaniment to our fish. A couple of the carrot slices were cut too thickly, and were therefore uncooked, and their balsamic-brie dipping sauce did not contribute anything, but this is minor. We left the restaurant both sated and happy. We WILL return.
label: POS

text: Franny's - Home of the Throwed Rag You'll really just have to go to this place yourself to believe what I'm going to say. Harry put it perfectly when he said this place would provide all the fodder you'd ever need for a N'awlins cartoon strip. The decor is cheap circa 1970s, with panel-sided video poker cubbies added in. The scent alone is enough to knock you flat when you walk in; a combination of ancient food and bleach. Susan wanted to sit in a booth, and every vinyl bench she approached was wet from a recent wipe-down. A waitress yelled from across the room - "Just sit anywhere!!!!". When we said we couldn't sit on a wet booth seat - "They dry in a few minutes, just sit down!". Of course! Please understand, the place was almost empty. A dry rag couldn't make its way to the seats? No it couldn't, because they were closing in a half hour. Garnet, our waitress, was priceless. Somehow in the course of exchanging under 250 words, she actually said a sentence that contained the words "fried pig s***". Wow! Did I actually hear that?? Oh, I was ready for a hearty breakfast after that! Now, I will have to say that the coffee was decent. Don't go looking for decaf, though, because it's instant. We ordered a big breakfast, a pork chop breakfast, an order of eggs and hash browns, and the pecan waffle. Everyone's eggs were very runny, and the yolks were lemon-yellow. The color and water content of the yolk was indicative of a more cheaply produced egg, one where they definitely are not feeding the chickens extra Omega-3s for a healthy diet. While no pecans had ever seen the battter that constituted my "pecan" waffle, it was tasty! Had a somewhat nutty, whole-wheat flavor. It was cooked a bit too long, but it was by far the best thing anyone had on the table. The most hilarious moment came when Garnet delivered the syrup to our table. It was Value Time syrup. It surely must have been procured from Dollar Tree. It was a 48 oz. bottle of watery HF corn syrup. Hey, I asked for syrup, I didn't say what type! Susan suggested I ask again, but for maple syrup. I wonder what response that might have brought? Harry's bacon looked like it had been cooking under a flat iron for two hours. It was the flattest, driest bacon ever. But, in fairness, the guys ate every scrap of their breakfast meats, so I guess they're doing something right here. Garnet busied herself by taking every piece of dishware she could get from us as quickly as possible, since they were closing in 20 minutes. We all know the difference between good service or "get out of here" mode from a server. We were getting the treatment, that's for sure! The climactic moment came when a rag, doubtlessly the same rag that was used to wipe down our moist bench seats before we arrived, was catapulted practically across our table. The waitresses, Garnet and accomplice, could not waste a moment to exchange the rag between hands, otherwise how would they leave the building in five minutes? So, the rag flew past us at eye level to cover 4 yards before reaching its destination. Touchdown! Speaking of touchdowns, the entire decor, and playlist, of Franny's is New Orleans Saints-themed. We did enjoy singing "Who Let the Dogs Out" before we departed. Where was Nat'ly this morning? Where was Vic? They must have been there earlier.
label: NEG

text: Yesterday, April 5, 2011, I took my family on a ten hour, round trip drive from kentucky to Indianapolis to have a wonderful lunch at Jersey's Cafe. This story is about my bad experience at Jersey's Cafe. My wife, two and a half year old, six month old, and I are used to eating at all types of restaurants from pizza to medium dining. The kids were having fun, not making a scene, or being overly loud. In fact, another customer commented to my wife that we had cute kids, and we shared small conversation with the table next to us. I have worked in restaurants, as has my wife. After seeing Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives, and having reviewed their online menu, I decided to try the Westwood sandwich and their chicken salad sandwich with bacon. The steak sandwich looked amazing, and I eagerly wanted to let its rich flavors of steak, tomato sauce, meatball, cheese, and crunchy crusted roll (roll is "imported" from New York) wash over my senses and transform my lunch into Nirvana. I had high expectations. Sadly, I never even saw that steak sandwich. We got there at 3pm on that Tuesday. With kids, it's always best to aim for in-between meals, just in case. Their sign warns customers of a 30 minute wait from order to food and blame their success. Ok, whatever. It's made to order, not a problem... I can wait for good food. One waitress and one new buss-person was working the 45 seat (or so) dine-in area. I let my wife order our main reason for being there, and she ordered the big blue, and I told the waitress that we would each have one (oops, this was the wrong sandwich for me, but exactly what my wife wanted). Waitress suggested getting one of the big blue's and sharing it. Neither my wife nor I wanted to share because of the specialness of the long drive and the anticipation of a wonderful sandwich. This was not the Westwood which I wanted. Probably my fault for ordering the wrong sandwich. I'll grant the Jersey cafe that, but how a restaurant handles problems is as important as how they make food. We also ordered a $3 hot dog for my 2 year old and two drinks (another $4). After waiting every bit of half an hour, they brought the sandwiches, and I immediately told the buss-person, food carrier that there must be a mistake, that I ordered the steak sandwich. He called over the waitress and I repeated that I had ordered the steak sandwich on the big roll, covered in cheese... you know. We cleared up the issue, I had mis-ordered. I asked what we could do, because I did not want the sandwich in front of me. I didn't really want to wait another 30 minutes for the other sandwich, but the waitress was clear that ANY SOLUTION WOULD REQUIRE ME TO PAY FOR THIS SANDWICH. It turns out that no manager was there that afternoon, just cooks and waitresses: no supervisor/manager to appeal to. So, I asked if she would make me pay for a sandwich that I ordered and didn't like. She said, in no uncertain terms, that if I ordered it, I'd have to pay for it, regardless of anything about the sandwich. It's an $8 sandwich. So I told her that if I had to pay for a sandwich I didn't want, regardless of what I ordered or received, her tip would be used to pay for it. She got angry, made a comment, stormed off and it sounded like she either bumped something which fell, or threw something on her way into the kitchen. At that point, any tip to her was history. She ignored/avoided us the rest of our time there. I'm not rich, and I will not pay $6-10 tip for a meal that included an unsolved problem. I understand that people are picky, and often overly picky. Jersey Cafe's policy, though, transforms an otherwise decent eat-in deli into a lunch counter. Why pay a waitress to bring my food when they really want me to order at a counter, pay, get my food and negotiate problems with them holding the money, and me holding the food. That's the problem she and the restaurant creates with such a policy. She was calm when talking about a problem with my money. When I made the problem affect her money, she got angry and emotional. Interesting, huh? If a waitress cannot solve such problems when they come up because of restaurant policy, the restaurant shouldn't have serving staff: they should have counter staff. Were this sandwich joint to have had counter staff, she wouldn't have expected a tip, she never would have gotten personally involved, and I would have probably not expected her to be able to fix that problem. But I would have still asked and hoped they would have tried something to make me happy. I don't want anything for free. I just wanted to taste that steak sandwich, but was not going to pay double. Overall for the restaurant, I didn't want my money back, I didn't want something for free. I wanted their sandwich. I would have loved to have reviewed their food here, but because of the wait staff and Jersey Cafe's policy, this review is about the restaurant, not the food. I had a bad experience.

text: I've been getting my hair done at the Hair Suite for over ten years now. My mother was a client of a stylist that used to work there, and took me as a young teenager when I decided I wanted to dye my hair. In the years I've been a client my hair has gone from near platinum blonde to black and back to blonde, from elbow length to chin length and I have never ever left unhappy. Linda (a stylist and also the owner) is one of the nicest people you will ever meet and does a seriously fantastic job on my hair. She is straightforward and will let you know what is possible to accomplish in one session and will work with you to get the look you want. A few years back I got a little too friendly with my flat iron and broke off a giant chunk of hair right near my face. Linda gave me a cut that helped to blend it as it grew out and no one could even tell it was there! She is also great with color -- I get tons of compliments on my hair and owe it all to her. Back when myspace was the thing, someone found a picture of me and coincidentally brought it into the Hair Suite asking for my cut/color. As far as price -- I can't commit to a hairstyle or color for more than six months, so the price changes per visit but I don't think I have ever paid more than 160 including tip (cut, single process color, highlight, style). I moved to Philadelphia in 2007 and am in close proximity to several "high end" salons and still drive back to Cherry Hill to get my hair done. As long as they are open, I will continue to get my hair done at Hair Suite. Don't let the location or the fact that a big portion of the clientele are older women deter you -- I'll be honest, I am in my early-mid twenties and am almost always the youngest person in the salon. The atmosphere is a little lacking and the salon looks a little dated, but to be honest if these women operated out of a warehouse I wouldn't even care. They are that good!

There is a little takeout store on one side of the street and a very nice dining room on the other side. DELICIOUS. Truly a great meal. We got Thai rolls (similar to Vietnamese spring rolls), tom kha (chicken coconut soup), shrimp pad thai, and green curry with chicken. Everything was fantastic. The soup was a great sweet/sour combination, spring rolls were crispy and the ingredients tasted fresh. The shrimp were perfectly cooked on the pad thai and the green curry was creamy and spicy. They give you spice options for the main dishes - mild, medium, hot, or thai hot. I love spicy and can tolerate alot but the just plain hot on the pad thai was plenty. Anyone even a tiny bit wary of spicy, I would recommend go medium or mild. Price is average - around $33 (before yelp deal) for everything we got. BYOB - great with beer. Service is great. Portions are enormous, and everything reheats beautifully.

text: I go to pubs to eat and drink. Both of those worked out well. The discounted early beers were $4.50 a pint, the full price ones were $5.50. No kinks even though they have only been open for a few weeks. Both appetizers were good-- homemade chips with garlic aioli and Devil's on Horseback. The main courses my table shared were also above expectation. The fish and chips were both good, the beef and puddings were well presented, at the right temperature,and tasty and the chicken pie was substantial. The service was friendly and attentive. Everyone on staff we met was a cheerful booster. Good to see. The crowd while we were there was low on both pretence and irony. That, I would wager is par for the course at an English pub and the delivery of a happy crowd, both patrons and staff is more important than whatever defects the decor had. I think the decor was fine, if a little minimalist and bright. I sure wouldn't want to decorate a restaurant, let alone an English Pub in Nashville. Eveyone has their idea of how it should look. I can tell you how a hot chicken shack SHOULD look like; I live in this town and know it well enough. But being 4,000 miles from authenticity makes having the RIGHT idea vary wildly. Add to that Yelp, where everyone is an expert (lord knows I am) and you really can't win for losing. Glad they didn't invest too much in that fool's errand. text: I went here for the first time about two weeks ago, on the day Marathon Motor Works had that craft show thing that you pretty much couldn't get into. That visit, in my eyes, was an unmitigated disaster. The coffee was awful. Awful. A-W-F-U-L!!! The service was nonexistent, and there just wasn't any room at all. If I had reviewed it after that first experience, it would have easily been one star. But after some reflection, I decided that it would be wildly unfair to review a new location under such stressful circumstances. Not that it wouldn't be fun to write an unfair review; it would be wildly fun. Some of my favorite reviews were borderline unfair. But, once again, I have my integrity to think of. We also have to consider the fact that reviews can, for better and for worse, affect the affairs of businesses. Writing an unfair review out of vengeance might bring me laughs, but it might also cause an interested coffee fan to look elsewhere when this business might be just what they'd love, and my conscience can't bear that. So, to be fair, I visited twice more, and it's actually pretty darn good. The proprietor is a friendly, almost jovial middle-aged biker dude, who will chat you up and even have a word and a smile for your kids. I like that. The coffee is good when it's not rushed, and it's pretty clear the people behind the business cared greatly about making a good cuppa joe. Good baked goods, creative (though not very comfortable) seating helps, too. My main issue with the place is the extreme inconvenience. Marathon Village is hard to get to from one block away, much less downtown, or even Charlotte Pike. There's almost no direct route, leaving one to navigate several awkward turns. Parking is odd, too. Mostly, I've parked in the small empty field across the street, but even that seems frustrating. Finally, the bathroom feels like it's a quarter mile away. When my almost four year old asks to go to the bathroom everywhere we go, that's a headache. So the coffee is good and the experience is rewarding, but the effort it takes to get it is the biggest flaw Garage has. C'est la vie...

text: It's no wonder that Franklin Mortgage & Investment Co is so highly acclaimed. Then you descend the steps into an unassuming black door (no windows) and you enter a different era. The servers are wearing plaid shirts, jeans, and suspenders. The room is dimly lit with a few tables and a bar top. Now you see why the line is worth the wait. The crowd control at the door means a relaxed, non-crowded experience at the bar. And you never get rushed out. As for the drinks, they come pretty strong, with lots of citrus flavors, cucumbers, mint, and other delicious concoctions. If you don't want something on the menu, get it off the menu, or ask the bartender to make you something you might like. I had the Emma Frost and the Killer Bees on the Swarm. Both citrus, both tasty, the Killer Bees a bit more heavy on the tequila. Sometimes it's nice to escape from modern day Philly and have an expertly made drink in a different era. Like I said, definitely worth the wait.

text: Life just would not be the same without Verti Marte. What makes this convenience store so special? Well, in a word, EVERYTHING! This place is the epitome of one stop shopping and absent being told of this place, you would peg it for a 24/7 neighborhood grocery store. While it is a 350 sq ft neighborhood store, it is also some of the best take out food you will ever eat in the New Orleans for a reasonable price. I literally crave their po-boys and Mac n cheese. And when I'm in the mood for something else, I stare into the front display case and select my items as if I am in a cafeteria style line. While the food is reasonably priced, it has a few "hidden costs". It is take out only, parking is hard to find, it is cash only and it seriously takes anywhere from 15-20 minutes for preparation, warming or whatever they are doing to complete each order. The wait is frustrating because there is very little standing room. You will slide past others and adjust to let others by while you are waiting. But know this. It is totally worth dealing with! VM has the goods! A po-boy is not a po-boy without Leidenheimer bread. Verti uses Leidenheimer. While I am overly obsessed over their All the Jazz po-boy, I out a few of the others in heavy rotation. I am a fan of their grilled shrimp po-boy, the royal feast, Hot Sausage with Cheese and their Philly Chicken po-boys too. VM has amazing turkey burgers and grilled cheese sandwiches too. If you are a fan of special sauces, add their wow sauce to your order. It'll have you moaning and saying wow, this is so good (.... in my Frank Davis voice). If you are in the FQ area and can not or will not visit the store, you have another option. Verti offers delivery service. While I am often in a position to order delivery, I admittedly enjoy the cramped up, wait in line experience because I appreciate the deliciousness all the more. Bon appetite!

text: Anthropologie came onto my radar when I watched the show "Man Shops the Globe" on the Sundance Channel awhile back. Kevin is one of the primary scouters for Anthropologie and he travelled the globe to places such as South Africa, Syria,Denmark, Turkey,Rome, London, etc., to seek out the most unique and special pieces for Anthropologie stores world-wide. The program really delved into the purchasing process and the philosophy of Anthro. Kevin always purchased items that were not made in child labour factories and he always went for items that were made by artisans and craftsmen who were singularly employed. Now having said that, the products featured on this show were obviously not all of the products that are in an Anthro. as evidenced by the WEM Anthro. location. It does appear that Anthro. stocks other items outside of the "Man Shops the Globe" scope and this is where the appeal of Anthro. may break down. Some of the items such as the jewellry appear to be made cheaply but they ask a lot for them. These are the type of items that you can get at a market stall for one fifth the price of Anthro. The WEM location is definately worth a look, the store has a clever staging and marketing scheme and it really appeals to my sense of art, culture and design. I liked the items displayed here and most definately plan to go back, while I might not be a great purchaser of most of their items, I know that I can get really good design and decorating ideas.

text: The essence of local. You get a choice from a few main dishes and two sides. The menu is limited but what they offer has excellent flavor right up there with the big name restaurants but at a fraction of the price. We had the fried fish which was catfish that day and crawfish étouffée. We tried all four side dishes, potato salad, peas, green salad and Mac & cheese. My wife lived in New Orleans for ten years and the catfish was as good as it gets, crispy and moist and the tartar sauce was some of the best she's ever had. The crawfish étouffée was outstanding, tender and nicely spiced. All the sides were good but the potato salad was great with lots of chopped hard boiled eggs and celery and the Mac & cheese was nice and cheesy and not gritty. Oh, did I mention the fresh home made cookies? We had two peanut butter cookies that were moist and really pea nutty. Way too much food to eat and our total with drinks was $17 for two. Don't expect white table cloths and linen napkins. The atmosphere is paper plates and plastic forks and drink out of the bottle. There are only five tables and most folks do take out. This is a down to earth real New Orleans neighborhood place to relax with really friendly locals and enjoy some great food at an incredibly good price, and it's air conditioned.

text: Saturday, 12/18/2010 - 8pm reservations for two Went here for dinner with my special girl. She'd been dying to come here for some time, but I admit I was a little apprehensive given my hit-or-miss luck with upscale / "fine dining" restaurants. Plus I scoped out the menu online before going and nothing really stood out for me (forgive me for being a simpleton, but I don't know what half the things on these types of menus mean haha). The ship itself has a lot of history, and was very elegantly decorated (despite some comments in other reviews). It definitely feels like a place for a special night upon entering. Dinner starts out with complimentary rolls w/ butter. We then ordered a side of mac n' cheese and the moo shu duck for appetizers. The mac n cheese had a truffled crust and was served at a very good temperature (warm). Though it looks small, the serving size was good to split between two as an appetizer. Both the mac n cheese and moo shu duck were very good. She had the Maine Diver Scallops, which was voted 2010 Philly Cook's Dish of the Year. I tried some and it was very good. My Wild Mushroom Crusted Mahi Mahi was a bit dry though. The serving size for my Mahi Mahi was large and unexpected given the type of restaurant ("upscale"). We closed dinner with the Moshulu Coupe. I'm going to describe it as a vanilla ice cream w/ bits of chocolate "cake" that was very good (the simpleton in me). Service was very good. Definitely felt our waiter was attentive but not overbearing. I definitely enjoyed Moshulu, and the ambiance was probably a large part of why (very romantic). It just feels like a special place for a special occasion. The food was overall very good, though very disappointed with my entrée (the Mahi Mahi was dry). The price is actually very reasonable with all things considered. Appetizers from $8 up, entrees from $14-$20, dessert $10. You do have to pay for parking ($10??), but I believe that is typical for the area. I'd love to come back when the weather is good enough to eat and/or hang out on the boat's deck. Highly recommended. Overall 4.5 stars (rounded up to 5). (SEE PHOTOS FOR FOOD)

We started with the ricotta appetizer, which we loved so much that when the server and manager came over to our table we asked just what was in it, and the manager went so far as to ask the kitchen for the recipe. That was impressive and set the tone for the rest of the meal, which included the duck ravioli (it wasn't quite ravioli but I can't remember the name), wild boar pappardelle, and marscapone/pumpkin gnochhi with brown butter sauce. We were pretty full and completely satisfied but still couldn't say no to dessert, which was delicious but ultimately more than we needed. In hindsight we could have shared a single serving of gelato, because FYI it came plated in three separate scoops. But we regret nothing! This place made me miss Philly more than I already do, and will definitely be where I force people to go every time I have dinner when I'm in town. For about $15 you can get a 60 minute personal training session with a group of 4-6 other women. (A great way to make friends if you are new to the area or if you are just looking to make friends!) When the gym gets busy (especially in January) the cardio floor can get busy so it is important to be flexible in your exercise routine. I don't ever mind. text: I found Lakeview Movers on Craiglist and called, not sure what to expect. Shawn was incredibly friendly and professional. I told him that I was moving out of a studio apartment, and had a bed, loveseat, desk, dresser, and bookcase. He asked how many boxes I had and I had to confess that I had no idea, as I was still working on packing. He quoted me $170 and we made an appointment for 12:30. On the day of the move, he called around 9:40 am and said that another client had cancelled, and asked if I'd like to move my appointment up. That worked for me! We arranged for 11. He showed up right on time with another guy and his truck. They also had plenty of truck blankets, plastic wrap, dollies, and other professional equipment- this was not two guys with a truck trying to make some extra cash, this is a professional moving company. I showed them the furniture and said that if they had extra room for the boxes and other stuff, that would be awesome, but that really if they could just take care of the heavy furniture, that would be fine, since I could come back and get the rest in my car. And since they had a pickup truck instead of a huge U-Haul type truck, I didn't really think that much would fit. Boy, did they prove me wrong! They fit almost my entire apartment in the back of that pickup truck. It was like watching Ultimate Tetris. :) They stacked and fit boxes and furniture and random crap together, but in a way that was very secure and made me totally comfortable. They had it down to a science. Then they padded everything with blankets and strapped everything down with bungee cords. There was no way that anything was going anywhere! When we got to the new place, unloading was quick and easy. They were really great about asking where I wanted everything. Overall, it was a really great experience, and well worth the money. They were both super friendly and respectful of my belongings, and they went above and beyond to make my move a much less stressful experience! I would definitely recommend them. :)

text: This is a must try spot. This is the sort of restaurant that you might passby and not give a second thought to it. El Tule has an expansive menu -- one Peruvian and one Mexican. My companion ordered a vegetarian lasagna from the Mexican menu. I ordered from the Peruvian menu. What a treat to be able to eat authentic recipes from Peru right here in Lambertville! The owners themselves, a brother and sister, are Peruvian. The food is freshly and wonderfully prepared. My order was photograph worthy, in fact, arriving on two plates each skillfully plated as an edible work of art. On one dish was Ceviche de Camarones: "Close your eyes and enjoy this treasure of a ceviche that will take you back to my cherished Peruvian cost. Our succulent shrimp ceviche is marinated in lime juice, garlic and aji amarillo served with red onions, sweet potatoes, Peruvian corn and Inca corn." On the other dish was a trio: Yuquitas Fritas with Huncaina Cream: "Crunchy fried yuca sticks served with a natural Andean cream made from milk, cheese and the secrets of Huncayo." Causa de Pollo: "Yellow potato cake inspired from a native land of the Inca. Enriched with yellow peppers and magical lemon, stuffed with chicken and vegetables and seasoned with Peruvian spices." Palta A La Reina: "Half of an avocado stuffed with shrimp, red onions, tomatoes and corn. Marinated with fresh cilantro-lime dressing." My meal was a little pricey at $27 but totally worth it. The wonderful flavors are still lingering in my mouth as I write. There is absolutely a selection of lesser priced items on the menus. My friend's Lasagna de Vegetales "Sautéed Eggplant, Zucchini, Roasted Red & Poblano Peppers, Mushrooms, & Queso, Layered Between Spinach Tortillas & Baked Until Golden Brown" was only $12. I had a taste and it was delish and very different from the better known Italian Lasagna. Wash your meal down with "Jaicama" (I believe the spelling is correct), a house drink that El Tule makes with hibiscus flowers. I will defiantely be back in the Spring to take advantage of the outdoor dining.

text: We wanted to like Elevation Burger. We really, really did. And even if you factored out the employee at the cash register who acted like a complete idiot, the food was soooo disappointing. If you're going to specialize in burgers and charge high-end prices for them and use supposedly good beef, then why on EARTH are you NOT going to season the patties? Unseasoned meat makes for dull flavor. And if you're going to use grass-fed beef which, generally, has a lower fat content than your average CAFO beef, then WHY are going to cook the bejeezus out of your burgers. Dry doesn't even begin to describe the $6 burger we ordered. And then, let's talk about the fries. The boy and I were amused to read that they fry the fries in olive oil. I know that there's the whole "olive oil" is healthy craze in America and everyone and the mother thinks that EVOO (with a Rachel Ray Ee-Voh pronunciation) is a god sent answer to all that ails your poor french-fry eating heart, but it's not. Olive oil, especially the cheapo (as in quality, not price) Bertolli Olive Oil we saw stored under the counter is not designed to handle the high heat of frying fries. Olive oil has a pretty low smoke point and if you heat olive oil to the temp you need to reach to fry potatoes to crispy perfection, well then, you're creating carcinogens in that there oil. So here's your "healthy" fries with a side of cancer. But we might even be able to forgive that basic culinary flub IF our fries had not shown up with so many burned bits. Well, first, they didn't show up at all. I know the joint was hoppin' with all four us in there, but to forget the fries and then to check the ticket like I was lying when I said that we ordered fries, well, that's just annoying. But to have the fries arrive with acrid-tasting burned bits on all of them, well, that's just bad frying. And not even the overly-cinnamoned Orange-Cinnamon iced tea could get that taste out of our mouth. If I wanted a dry, underseasoned burger with uninspired toppings and burned fries, I'd just go to Champ's across the way. I don't generally want that and I had such high hopes for a burger place that calls itself Elevation. As a tip for the owners, mosey on down to Center City and see how 500 degrees does it and then mosey on back to Collegeville and look at implementing some of their methods. And season your burger patties for crying out loud. You're not doing yourselves, your beef or your customers any favors by playing hide-and-seek with the salt and pepper.

text: I've been to the jube several times for touring musical productions. I love the stadium seating, it's really hard to get a bad seat here - unless someone who's super tall sits in front of you. There are two balconies. The first balcony is really great, but I find the higher balcony harder to see from. The lobby is nicely decorated, with lots of local art. The drinks here are overpriced, so I tend to just go out somewhere after the show. The bathrooms are always clean, but get really busy. I don't like how the soap is integrated into the faucet system (unless that's been changed recently). It just means you're never 100% sure how clean your hands are, or your left with that soapy residue on them. As far as acoustics go for the audience they are great. The sound is quite good, and you won't have a problem hearing anything. I can say when I sang here I found the accoustics weren't great - this is for those performing, not the audience. But perhaps they were able to make some improvements with renovations. Still acoustically I don't think it compares to the Winspear Centre. Paid parking is available, but harder to come by with all the construction going on in the area. I would recommend taking the LRT where possible. The jubilee is a nice theatre in Edmonton, although it certainly doesn't have a classic feel to it, the way a theatre in New York would. Still unless your here for a rock concert I'd recommend getting dressed up. Nothing formal, just something nice. I always hate when I see people with ripped jeans and grubby t-shirts. Why not put on something clean if you're going for a night out?

text: Nothing I or anyone else says about this place will make any difference, so I might as well have a bit of fun with it. If this was a review of a tourist trap, it would get 4, maybe 5 stars. But it isn't. This is a tourist trap which happens to serve beef produced by the cattle company that owns it. You don't come here because you think this is actually a good place to eat steaks. If you do, I genuinely feel sorry for you. You come here for the touristy stuff, or because kids like it (this was my particular excuse this time). I could come up with a whole laundry list of reasons why you shouldn't come here. So what the hell, I'll give you a list: o Haphazard management of the waiting list. My small group was the only one waiting to eat the night we were there (highly rare occurrence). We were told it would be a "short wait". 15 minutes later, 2 groups of the same size came out of nowhere and were seated before us. It would have been nice if they told us a few groups of the same size were already on the list. But they didn't have buzzing coasters and we did... Conspiracy theory? There is always some problem with people waiting here though. o The place is huge, but even if there are a million empty tables, they won't seat you right away. I expect this is because they are pinching pennies and not bringing in enough servers. o The menu does not list the sizes (weights) of the steaks. So you have no idea what you're getting. This is an insult to you, the customer. They expect you to pay for whatever they give you. Fortunately, the price matches what they serve, but why force me to ask? o The steaks are just chunks of beef. There's nothing particularly redeeming about them other than they are cooked over real fire. But that's the way they are meant to be cooked in the Wild West. Do yourself a favor and get steaks from your local butcher, spend $30 on a cheap grill and some wood, and be happy with yourself for doing a better job than this. o The salad served in a big dish to make it look bigger than it is, and it's half filled with what I call "iceberg stumps". The stuff they don't use at their other restaurants maybe? o The bread. The only positive. Barely. o The beans. The beans are drowning in water, and no bowls to serve them in. I'm supposed to put them on top of my steak maybe? Or in my used salad bowl? How do beans and bleu cheese taste? I'll have to try that next time I have $40 burning a hole in my pocket. I can't think of any more right now. Maybe next time.

text: The fairly sudden passing of a family member brought us the difficult question of where would be the best place to carry out the final wishes and internment. Several of us had visited Curlew Hills and were impressed by the beautiful grounds and options for internment. When we contacted Curlew Hills, we were guided through the decision making process by their representative, who gave us thoughtful and useful recommendations while always considering the budget and other constraints of the decisions. For instance, while the family wanted a memorial service at a church for a large audience, afterwards Curlew Hills provided a small setting chapel viewing before internment for family and close friends at no cost. This small touch was greatly appreciated, and helped greatly through this difficult process. We also came to appreciate the universal kindness shown by every single employee of this family-owned business. I've never seen a more beautiful setting for a final resting place than Curlew Hills. And while I've never been one to visit remains at a cemetery, the gorgeous tree-shaded park-like setting is so peaceful it invites you to stop in for a time for thoughtful reflection. The grounds are so nice it's not unusual to see one or more visitors bring a lawnchair to sit in or even bring a small picnic. And the fact it's so safe and open 24/7 makes a visit at any time not just possible but inviting. I've stopped by at midnight, and the quiet of a star-filled night was a special moment. Curlew Hills is big enough to have different sections that are separated by different amenities, but those sections are small enough to always make it feel intimate. In short, it just feels right. text: I see all the favorable reviews, so I'm reluctant to swim against the tide. However, I ordered the bento box lunch special, and I wasn't impressed. The meal came with miso soup and a small salad topped with some gloppy salad dressing the same color as a prison jumpsuit. I didn't touch the salad. I interpreted the international orange coloring as a warning sign. (CORRECTION: It's made with carrot. It's supposed to be orange. Ignore me.) Two spoonsful of the soup told me all I needed to know about it. Bland and watery. The bento came with long skewers of breaded shrimp, but honestly all I could taste was the cooking oil. The dumplings were mushy, with plenty of cabbage but nothing much else. The California rolls were fishy, even for sushi. I have eaten there once before. I had the pad thai, which for a suburban restaurant was pretty good. I suspect I've just tried something they don't do nearly as well.
label: NEG

text: The pizza, as expected, was amazing. Get the vegetarian wheat crust. You won't regret it. They were gracious enough to keep the kitchen open a bit longer for us even though we showed up very closely to the kitchen (not the bar or the restaurant) closing time. The staff is your basic hipster type with questionable customer service skills and an impaired memory. That's the reason for 4 stars. If the guy in super skinny jeans and an artsy haircut who was serving us actually cared about his customers, it would have been a perfect experience.
label: POS

text: So, I hate to sound like a snob, but most people really don't know how to buy the right pair of jeans. It sounds trivial (and it is) but it's true and pretty important if ya want to look good! It's like buying a bra, most women are buying the wrong size, and when they finally get fitted and realize they've been wearing the wrong size all these years, it's kind of a bummer. I'm speaking from personal experience. It's all about learning what cut fits your body type best, the length, your waist size, how much the pant will stretch, and the list goes on. So I pretty much feel the same way about buying jeans and bras: get fitted! I got schooled on everything denim the first time I went to Loop several years ago. The price point at Loop may be high, but buying your denim here is totally worth it. I've always been satisfied with my purchases at Loop because the owners (name) make 100% sure that you are buying the right pant for your body. These people know the ins and outs of the perfect fit and it's very clear that it is very important to them that you leave their store feeling like a rock star. Their attention is all yours when you're shopping in their store. There are few places in Tucson that provide such a personalized and fun shopping experience, so support the independent guys! I highly doubt anyone at Dillards is going to make sure you LOVE LOVE LOVE every purchase you make. Next time your near Casas Adobes pop into Loop, you won't regret it!
label: POS

text: This place strikes as a straight okay for me. I would never pick it myself, but I'm not going to grumble and complain if someone I'm with wants to go there. I've gone 2 or 3 times and each time has been pretty consistent. The bartender is extremely nice, and remembered me after only being there once before! The service is a little iffy, but that's because every time I've gone they've clearly been understaffed. I've really only ever seen the bartender seriously working. (Once, however one of the servers told us that she was covering for someone but too drunk to work. Now I'm not sure if she was kidding or not, but huh?) I really like the mystery beer thing, but I wish I could get something better more often (if you have to raise the price from $3 to $4 and I was getting not as many Miller High Lifes and various Yuengling that'd be great) Fries were pretty delicious but the rest of their food (tuna steak sandwich, kind of bland, and chili) were acceptable but not exceptional. Don't recommend the Quizzo here either, it needs some work.
label: NEG

text: Absolute best sushi I had in my life. Waitresses are not very friendly and drinks are so so but the sushi is the best. Try the birds nest roll. YUM!

text: Since I live in the neighborhood, I find myself at Green Line quite often. The coffee is quite delish and that's high marks from this coffee snob. I typically hate fair trade (sorry y'all), but for some reason, theirs is really effing good. What I REALLY love is their teas. I have yet to find a Moroccan mint that even comes close to theirs. I've had a few of the pastries and they are delish. The everything bagel is well worth the calories as well. The inside is cute with pretty awesome and constantly changing artwork from local artists. Also, the manager Dave is a super nice guy.
label: POS

text: I went here for lunch during the week. First of all the exterior looks shady, but the interior is very nicely decorated. The ambiance is great. The service was prompt. I also really enjoyed the complimentary miso soup, edamame (about a cup's worth), and small scoop of plum ice cream. It really rounded out my meal! I had a spicy tuna roll, a specialty roll, and a house salad. The rolls were good - the fish tasted fresh, and the ingredients melded well together. Definitely skip the house salad - the dressing isn't as good as I've had at other Japanese restaurants, and it was just plain iceberg lettuce. Other than the house salad, the food was high quality and tasty. Will definitely be going back!
label: POS

text: YUM! Best Indian in town- I had a meal with 6 people and we ate almost everything on the menu (well not almost, but close!) The chicken tikka was incredible- we had leftovers and they were devoured the next day. The Lamb Shank Korma was also to die for- the flavors were out of this world. I had a shrimp dish that was great once I dunked my shrimp in a little sauce. All of the sides: cauliflower, eggplant and mixed vegetables were excellent. The garlic naan was doughy but delicious...just the way I like naan! I will be back- It's amazing indian food. YUMMO!

Second time we were here, The first time they brought half t table's dinner and 20 minutes later brought the rest! Not how we want to spend our leisure time! We left and went to McDonalds!

Cost was very reasonable... the one pizza and appetizer left two very hungry people very well fed. We'll be back!

text: Friends took me to Peter's while I was visiting Nashville. From the outside, it doesn't look like anything special. It doesn't look bad or unappealing but it's in a strip mall and I probably wouldn't have stopped there on my own. That would have been my loss. The food at this place is AMAZING. We ordered a bunch of stuff and shared everything. It's been over a week ago, and my memory is crap, so I can't recall exactly what we had. For me, the standout was the green dragon roll (tres yummy). Everything we had was so good. Were I a Nashville local, Peter's would totally be one of my go-to spots. If you've never been there, go. Now.

text: Just popped in for a drink or three and ordered a dirty martini. Yes, I realize that this is a Spanish restaurant but that's what I was in the mood for. It was outstanding! Arguably one of the best dirtys I've had in some time. Another notable drink was an Alma Blanca (white silk). We noticed the bartender, Genardo, muddling some corn, habenero, lime, and some other ingredients which arroused our curiosity. We HAD to have one of these mysterious drinks. Genardo served the drink which was cloudy in appearance almost milky looking. Given the habenero incorporation, I thought this was going to have quite a kick. To my disappointment it was not spicy; however, it was quite the amazing drink and worth having again. The last drink was made by a bartender who was quite the character. His name was Vinny who first claimed to be Mexican but shortly after that he revealed that he was actually Italian. He subsequently asked my name but first took a few guesses: Biff, Chad, [insert stereotypical cocky blond-haired guy's name]. Of course, I never took offense to this as it was all in fun and gave us all a good laugh. As a kind reward for his brief roasting, Vinny offered to make us a special "off the menu" drink on the house. It was called: Hot Pickel. Now this drink was HOT!!! The drink consisted of basil, lime, tequila, cucumber, and jalepeno. It was spicy yet refreshing and I WILL make it back there very soon for another. Overall, this was a great experience for a quick stop for drinks. The staff were very fun to be around and the service was outstanding.
label: POS

text: I live in the neighborhood, and I really want to like Sun Ray, but as an epicurian I just can't recommend it. While the foods like the quesadilla and the Thai ribs have plenty of flavor, you can tell that it all comes from the seasonings the cooks use, and I get the feeling like the food may start as Sysco products. I don't sense any subtle blending of food flavors, but rather the tastes tend to clobber you with seasonings. The staff is friendly, and the food comes quickly, and the ambiance is slightly up-scale. If you only eat here once you'll probably enjoy it, but it's not the sort of place I return to again and again.
label: NEG

text: I love this place! The ambiance is very warm and welcoming, and the staff is very courteous, prompt, and attentive. The food is great and they were happy to make some simple modifications to accommodate my brother who is a vegan. I had a zebra stripe latte and it was absolutely amazing! I can't wait to go back and try more of their food and coffee selections. The pricing is also very reasonable. Definitely go here!

text: Everyone who likes to spend under $30 for a pedicure will typically have their favorite hole-in-the-wall spot to go. For years I was loyal to a place not too far from my house (comparatively, since I live in North Marana) because they were competent... and close. My friend introduced me to Campbell Spa about a year and a half ago. Campbell (north of Grant, east side of street, in same strip as Blackjack pizza) was quite a long trip for me from home, and it isn't exactly convenient from my place of work either, so I thought this might be a one-time trip for the sake of hanging out with a friend. First thing that surprised me? The price. $20 for a pedicure is a good price. But when you find out that includes a free design... that's a GREAT price. You heard me. One free design on each big toe. Most other places would charge you $30-32 for the same services together. But for $20, they have to do a cheap job, right? On the contrary! These folks are good. Not the best, but for the price, very very good. Staff is friendly, and remembers you from when you've been there in the past. They've got the standard massage chairs, and plenty of great staff. Why are they missing the final star, then? Well, they could use the higher standards of cleanliness... like a removal filter that gets cleaned between uses, and regulars getting their own set of supplies. Also, they are often busy (being so close to the U of A) and even when I call ahead I still end up waiting. All that said, it's a great place for the price and service... even worth a long trip from Marana!
label: POS

text: We've been attending FVC for 3 year now and we plan to go year after year. It's a great place for adults to have adult time (wine tasting, bike riding, dinner downtown without kids, or just plan old down town) while the kids have their own activities. The kids enjoy their activities with counselors which include field trips to the zoo, a local farm, maritime museum, touch pools on campus; fun playing at the beach; singing songs (and ours keeps singing the songs for many months after we leave) and just plan having fun!! Of course there is family time from working together to make derby cars, painting ceramics, playing bingo, enjoying a family carnival where everyone can participate and just hanging out as a family doing a bike ride, checking out the beach, swim at the pool or explore Santa Barbara. The food is great and kid friendly. From a stir fry bar, wood burning brick oven for pizza, salad bar, variety of breakfast items and fresh fruit. One would think that staying in a dorm room, eating college campus food isn't the greatest thing in the world but we compare our time with FVC like a cruise - you've got a great staff, entertainment, food, lodging and great times for the entire week and you don't have to get sea sick!!
label: POS

text: I had a bad feeling about this place, but it was late and everything else was closed, closing, or a noisy bar which we were not up to. The decor looks like a 4 year old's dream come true. The menu and table had a certain stickiness to them. My entree was simple enough: an "Apple Harvest Salad." Sounds appealing, no? Well it was absolutely disgusting. The chicken was clearly a frozen patty that had been warmed up in a microwave and then lightly seared on the grill. It was tough and had no taste whatsoever. I literally took one bite and pushed it aside. The "salad" was the stuff you buy in bulk at BJ's or Costco. Nothing more than iceberg lettuce. As if that wasn't insulting enough, the tough whitish core of the lettuce was nestled right under the chicken. My H's sandwich (Prime Rib Dip) was slightly better, then again, he was starving. I thought it was tough too. The fries were the only saving grace, but they were only slightly warm. Ugh. Stay away. I wish I could give ZERO stars.
label: NEG

Tucson can get too hot at times, but the Pozole and Cheese soup are excellent here, you just have to try them. Enjoy!

text: This place is truly awful, and my experience here was mediocre at best. A friend and I arrived in Nashville and had a few hours to kill before driving to Memphis. We found Tavern on Yelp, and in light of the good reviews, thought we would give it a try. Our first impression was not good, and should have been a sign to run for our lives over to Mellow Mushroom. We walked in and were promptly greeted by two hostess types. When they told us the wait would be 45 minutes, we pointed to the several empty tables on the patio (not to mention the empty tables INSIDE) and we asked if we could just sit outside. Their response: "Oh, we seat all the tables in ORDER, so it doesn't matter where you sit." Seriously? Have you ever been to a restaurant, say, EVER?? We figured we were already here, so might as well wait it out. We went over to the bar, and what do you know?! It's 2 for 1 cocktail night. So we order two cool-sounding drinks from the special menu, and they arrive promptly. The check comes, and we are informed that your SECOND is free. A classic bait-and-switch: it isn't "2 for 1," it's "buy one drink and then your second drink is free." But when we told the bartender that we had a three hour drive ahead of us and we weren't planning on a second drink, he was cool and just charged us for one. The drinks were terrible. Mine tasted like a Ricola and hers just tasted bad. The bar was extremely crowded and loud, and full of "dude-bro" types. FINALLY we were seated. I ordered the Israeli bread salad and she got the lobster sliders. Apparently by "toasted olive bread" in my salad they actually just meant croutons from a box. My friend's "lobster" (let me get out my microscope here) sliders cost $21. They came with chips, which, upon inspection, appeared to be plain old crinkle cut kettle chips. You know, from the bag. A complete and total waste of money. Maybe this is what passes for a cool night out in Nashville, but this place wouldn't stay open for 3 second in my native Los Angeles.
label: NEG

text: It's not the Ritz or the Roosevelt, but it's a good, moderately upscale hotel with a great location. However, that location *is* Bourbon Street & Canal, so arrive with certain expectations: Acme & Krystal and brass bands right outside your door. Hustler club, drunktards, and that fetid Bourbon street smell as well. I'm pretty confused by the really negative reviews here. We came in for Jazz Fest and had a great stay. Our room was large, clean, and the air conditioning worked great. Heeding advice here, we requested a room in the tower & got it. We could hear the bands on bourbon, but nothing that woke us up. Doors & walls are pretty thin. This hotel does trend older, so don't expect to whoop it up here. Even though most were in for Jazz Fest, we saw a number of well heeled folks throughout our stay. We also saw a number of nola amateurs. So, If you're looking for an in-hotel party scene, I'd recommend le cirque, the W, Hilton, or Harrahs. Or, really, just leave it on the street. Not like the bars & clubs ever close. To those well-heeled clientele, this hotel is at the corner of Bourbon & Canal, expect some shenanigans or go to the Roosevelt, Lafayette, or Ritz. Pool was adequate. Bourbon Milk Punch was tasty. Complimentary febreeze to get the smoke smell from bars out of our clothes was a nice touch. Never ate at the restaurant. Had minimal exposure to the staff, but they seemed generally weary.
label: POS

text: I visited Berry Sweet on a scorching hot day after a visit to Magic Gardens. I was enticed by the sight of frosty beverages on a poster in the window. Once inside? No prices to be seen. No beverages to be seen. You grab a cup, dispense the froyo flavors of your choosing (I went with chocolate, vanilla and mint) and top it with whatever you like. Then you pay by weight. It's hard to get just a little yogurt. When you pull the handle, a significant amount comes out. I ended up with more than I wanted... and it's not like you can shove it back in the nozzle. As for the toppings, I shoveled in a few Oreo pieces. They tasted soft/stale. Unacceptable. The woman at the counter clearly hated her job. She was unpleasant. And when I got out into the hot sun, Berry Sweet's yogurt failed to impress my taste buds. There must be better options elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: A great local (regional chain) diner with friendly staff, serving up tasty comfort food in a clean and pleasant atmosphere. The menu offers a wide selection of breakfast and sandwich items, all reasonably priced. On a quest for a good meal from a non-chain restaurant, I searched Yelp and found Dot's. I'd driven past Dot's several times and thought about trying it, and now I'm glad I did. I found easy parking right on the corner, and was encouraged when I saw local law enforcement and taxi drivers dining here. Greeted when I entered, I decided to sit at the classic diner counter. The interior is nicely done in a semi-50's diner motif, with a fair amount of seating including booths and tables. Flat-panel TVs with CNN and ESPN gave you something to watch if the local color didn't somehow maintain your interest. The waitress promptly provided me with a menu and asked for my drink order, all the while greeting other diners as they came in, many by their first names (obviously a local favorite.) After reading about the Crawfish Julie (thanks Meli E.), I decided to have the seafood omelet with hash browns. Watching the cool looking cook whip up my omelet (she sure knew her way around the kitchen!), it was ready within a few minutes, and served with a buttermilk biscuit that was halved and then browned on the grill, a nice touch! My omelet was delicious, as were the hash browns. Despite my best efforts to limit how much I was going to eat, everything was so tasty I wound up eating it all. I checked out using a major credit card for under $10, and left with a satisfied smile on my face. I'll be back the next time I'm in the area!
label: POS

text: Great soft pretzels. Not like the stale, crusty variety that you see vendors (whose sanitary techiques are questionable I might add) push on the street corners. No, these are hot, airy, and soft. Each bite is pretzel perfection!

text: Grossly overpriced for average deli fare. I paid $12.29 for a hot brisket sandwich on my latest trip that was decent but nothing to write home about. They will also charge extra for fries and other add-ons. The place unsure whether it wants to serve you to-go or in house. If you order to go you are bound to wait a good 10 minutes and will have to awkwardly shuffle around other customers. If you are looking for a highly stacked pastrami on rye, you will be sorely disappointed. I have given this place three tries now because it is so conveniently located, but this latest trip will be my last. Go to Murrays or Hymies on Montgomery Ave. - better food and more value for your dollar.

I also had different drinks each of those times, I've had their Dunkachino, Vanilla Chai (which I usually love) and hot chocolate. They should be ashamed to sell drinks like this. Stay away from this Dunkin Donuts, the other locations are much, much better.

text: I'm not going to lie, I saw this place on 'Best Thing I Ever Ate' and wanted to come here to try the mashed potatoes, specifically. I don't even love mashed potatoes in general, but they sounded irresistible on the show, so I wanted to try it! So glad I did! My boyfriend took me here for a nice dinner on Saturday night. We made reservations for 9pm, so we got our table right away. It was a little rainy but on a nice night it would be beautiful to sit outside. It does have a very authentic European feel at Parc, which is one of the reasons I'm giving it high marks. But the main reason of course, is the food. It's delicious and yes, the mashed potatoes lived up to expectations and were super silky and delicious. We started with a cheese plate and some beers - yum. They also gave us lots of bread, but I didn't want to spoil my appetite! I figured I had a pretty nice sized portion coming my way for dinner, and I did. I ordered the roast chicken and it was super moist and flavorful! My bf got the lamb loin and it was cooked to a perfect medium rare and also very tasty. We opted for no dessert because we were totally full. Oh, and this place is not cheap. But well worth it in my opinion. I'm going to be craving and dreaming about this meal for awhile, and will definitely need to check out Parc for brunch as well!
label: POS

My mom gave some kids cupcakes for my birthday, and they actually confiscated them! The rooms were okay - they were very big which was nice. The food at the cantina was okay - a mediocre taco salad but the waitress was absolutely darling. Overall a meh experience - I would go with Atlantis over the Grand Sierra as a rule.

text: I'm torn between giving Grandma Tony's pizza a 2 or 3 star rating. The pizza itself wasn't very good. I mean, it kind of tasted like Costco pizza, and I hate Costco pizza. Their sauce seemed to be missing an ingredient that would give it any kind of taste. The cheese was liberal, but definately not fresh. The sausage was the kind I hate most: the pieces look like mouse droppings. We ordered boneless chicken bites, and they were pretty bad also. Heavily breaded, formed into chicken balls, no flavor. So, you may be asking, why would I even consider giving them 3 stars? Because they were cheap and fast. An XL 3 topping and the chicken bites delivered was only $22. But even affordability can't make me eat there again.
label: NEG

text: Hands down, the best B&B experience I have ever had. The other two reviews here pretty much cover it all - but, I can't say enough about the owners! Rob and Kevin were SO wonderful. They bent over backwards to be accommodating (we missed our connecting flight and got in late, for starters - they couldn't have been more gracious). I knew from the minute I spoke to Rob on the phone when we booked the reservation that I would like him - and I was right. Rob and Kevin make you feel at home and are genuinely nice, welcoming hosts without any pretense whatsoever. Colorful characters with impeccable taste? You bet! The love and care they have put into creating this charming property is evident from the minute you step through the front gate. The gardens, the decor, the attention to detail in making your stay comfortable are all part of what makes this a little slice of heaven. I love the neighborhood, too - you're easily within walking distance of the French Quarter, live music on Frenchman Street, great shopping on Royal St. too. And Rob's helpful tips on things to do (and NOT do) are spot on - trust him, he knows what he is talking about! There's a great place for breakfast/lunch (should you opt to sleep in and miss Rob & Kevin's early morning hospitality - a shame, but it happens!) right across the street on the corner called the Cake Cafe and Bakery. We miss it already and can't wait to go back!
label: POS

text: I have developed a nasty Forever New Orleans habit. Over the course of a 7 day stay in New Orleans, I went in to this store every single day. Some days I dropped in twice. The thing with this place is, every time you go in there, you find something you had missed before. It isn't that it is messy or disorganized, it is just chock full of the greatest NOLA trinkets, candles, books, hostware -- you name it. They also seem to have a constant turn over with their merchandise..so if you are eyeing a glass bottle with that fleur de lis toppper, you best buy it on the spot. It can (and will) get swooped up by somebody else! I happen to really love fleur de lis and this store really brings it with everything you can imagine with the fleur de lis florish without seeming tacky and overdone. Bottom line is this is the greatest gift store in the french quarter. You can't miss it, it is just across the street from Rouse's and always has live music playing out front.
label: POS

text: This place is absolutely great. I just moved to Philly and frankly have not been very impressed with many of the restaurants here. Well, this restaurant is only a few minutes from my house, so I thought I'd give it a try. We started with a bowl of tom yum soup (an absolute must any time I go eat Thai food), curry puffs, and shrimp golden (ie fried shrimp rolls). They were all fantastic. The curry puff was flaky and perfect. The tom yum soup hit all the right notes of spicy and sour. For our main, we had yellow curry fried rice and crispy duck with sweet and sour sauce. Both of them were great. Dessert was fried ice cream and it was good, although not the best I've ever had. It was still pretty high up there on my list. The service was terrific. We went late and the waiter showed no impatience or annoyance that we would keep him working a while longer. He was very sweet and inquired about our needs while being unobtrusive about filling our water and taking our plates. He seemed genuinely pleased that we were raving about the food. The prices were also reasonable. I've spent twice as much at other places for the same food without the same quality and service and would have happily spent that much to eat here. I was just about to give up on Philly having any good Asian restaurants. I'm glad to see I was wrong. I'm definitely be coming here regularly. text: Hadn't been to Lou Bocarrdi's in quite sometime. I remember coming in when the storms of 2006 had downed power to most of the city in the summer and it was one of the few places that was open. Walking in the place sports a lot of what I would call "character" but others may see as needing "repair". The door has a bar on it but you actually need to use the handle at the bottom to enter. It is a little unnerving attempting to open the door into the bar but it is something I'll remember in future visits. Since I was last here I don't know what exactly changed but the downstairs bar area and dining area seemed brighter and more open. I think there had to have been some work done to the dining area to the right of when you enter because of the paintings and the tables stationed there. I was warned by the waitress that it is quite cooler in that area of the restaurant during the winter months. I guess I really noticed the downstairs dining area because of the window that looks out onto the Southwest/Magnolia split. The bar looks like it is from the 30's or 40's and is typical for what you would find at most other places in the area. There was one TV in the place located above the bar. Past the bar when you walk in is a set of stairs and two small rooms with tables which I would consider the main dining area. I don't think any of the tables are larger than a 4 top which is OK in my book because this restaurant, to me, is more for an intimate setting than for large groups. The walls in the second room have really beautiful mural paintings on them, compound that with the dim lighting it is almost like you are in an old museum. The menu has something for just about anyone on it and at all different price ranges as well. We started off with some garlic cheese bread. I went with the Tortellini which, all of the pasta dishes and entrees come with a salad and my mother went with the Gnocchi. The salad was a typical Hill restaurant salad served with lots of provel cheese and was very good. The Tortellini was very good. You have the option of choosing red or white sauce and I took the white. It was very rich and creamy with mushrooms in it. Mom's Gnocchi was good with the red sauce but she did comment that the shrimp were very tiny in size. I tried a bite and thought it was very tasty aside from the size of the Shrimp. All in all, the service was excellent and our waitress was very friendly and we even chatted a bit as the place was kind of slow. I definitely will come back because of all of the things on the menu I wanted to try. Based on past experiences I have to say their pizza is also pretty good for a Saint Louis style.
label: POS

text: ***Disclaimer: Everything you are about to read is 100% true*** This is an establishment that's part of a corporation of subpar and inflated-priced restaurants/watering holes that are becoming a rampant plague in the Quarter. You can identify them by their near identical menus and the " I (fluer de lis) N.O." shirts their employees wear. This PARTICULAR establishment is one of the more offensive/dangerous ones. Its decor is alluring. That's what lured me in. The drinks are horrendously overpriced (comparable to Bourbon Street pricing), deceivingly prepared (The Absolut Bloody Mary is made with Aristocrat Well - HONEST TO GOD; I'VE SEEN IT HAPPEN), and, in the instance of specialty drinks, uninspired. Now onto the food. I've seen an assembly line in the back kitchen area prefabricating muffalettas. Boxes of frozen oyster packs and frozen shrimp packs line the garbage areas of not just this location but all their locations. And they have the gall to refer to their shrimp as "gulf shrimp" on their menu. This place and this establishment is built on a masquerade and trickery. They are presenting themselves as true Louisiana cuisine when they are truly anything but. Its places like these that I have to warn people about and DEFEND my city's culinary reputation from. Please, I beg you, go to any of the other AMAZING eateries and bars in the Quarter. Do not give these people a dime in any of their tourist traps. And finally, if you have had the misfortune of being served here and actually liked it, imagine what real New Orleans food tastes like.

text: I can't help but equate Stephen Starr restaurants to the World Showcase at Epcot in Disney World--exquisitely manicured imitations of a panoply of settings and cultures, all in walkable proximity. Walking into Dandelion, I thought, "Ah, good, he's finally constructed England." Opening the heavy wood door on the corner (which was roughly equal in weight to the Black Gate of Mordor), instead of walking in to an open space, we were instead greeted by a tremulous mass of bodies--the place was freaking packed. (It was about 9pm on a Friday.) Normally I have little patience for bellying up to a packed bar with no available seats, only to attempt to get the bartender's attention from afar (and below--it feels like whenever this situation occurs, that I am surrounded by NBA-height patrons, also vying for drinks). But we decided to give it a try. We were able to order drinks with relatively low effort, and we were very impressed with the drink menu. I got a couple of double-chocolate stouts, and my wife got a mixed drink called the "tatanka," which she loved. We eventually got seats near the bar and really enjoyed our evening there. Good drinks, cool crowd. Next time, I hope to order some food--the cheese board looked amazing. So, as we eagerly await Mr. Starr's construction of Norway, or his adding a boat ride to El Vez, I recommend that you check out this newest stop on the World Showcase.

text: While driving home from San Luis Obispo to Orange County, I had a tire blow out on me. I put my donut spare on and drove 15 miles to the nearest town, Goleta. I called every tire place in the Santa Barbara area. Only Bob Woolevers both sold used tires AND had a tire ("a tire" is literal as I was told they had only one) my size. I couldn't afford a new tire; I had no credit card with me and only $50 cash on hand-and I would have to use the remaining balance from a used tire purchase for gas. I was told on the phone they had one tire my size in stock and that it would be $30 total, balanced/mounted/installed. When I got there, the guy brought out one of the baldest tires I've ever seen. I was appalled and immediately pointed out the total lack of tread on the outside, but was told it was a good tire, if it was bad they wouldn't sell it. I proceeded to buy the tire for one reason only - I was stranded and had absolutely no choice. When my tire blew, it was late at night and all businesses were closed, forcing me to spend the entire night sleeping in my car waiting for morning until shops opened. Driving home on the donut spare wasn't an option, as I've read that it's dangerous; you can't really exceed 50mph and you should never drive more than 50-70 miles on it-I was easily twice that distance from home. As tire professionals, Bob Woolevers knew that tire should never have been sold, much less placed on a traveling motorist's vehicle (I'd mentioned I was on my way home to OC). This, in my honest opinion, was very unethical behavior on the part of Bob Woolevers' shop. I strongly recommend looking elsewhere-ANYwhere-if you are in need of a used tire or tires.
