text: I would give this place more stars but the service was less than acceptable. The ambiance was excellent. A smallish restaurant in an old home was very French. The welcome into the restaurant and to our table was nice. They have a nice menu that has small, medium and large portions. We opted to choose from the small and medium, and a bottle of wine. From the small menu, we ordered a green salad, the soup of the day (which was a puree or vegetables) and crab cake. From the medium menu, we ordered the hand rubbed ribs and the barbecued shrimp. That was the order. I did not ask, but was not offered the option, but I expected the salad would come first (split in plates), then the soup and crab cake was the next course, then the ribs and shrimp. The salad came, split in two plates and then the server put the soup in the middle of the table as if we were going to stretch our spoons to get the soup. By the time we finished the salad, and I went to try the soup, it was tepid. As I was working on the soup, the crab cake, ribs and shrimp came all at once. Needless to say, it damped the entire meal. I think restaurants need to understand the meaning of tapas or izakaya style dining because it makes not sense to serve all the dishes at once, especially if there are only TWO PEOPLE! The whole idea of this type of dining is to take one's time to enjoy each dish. I was SOOOOO disappointed because these small things can ruin such a great experience. I certainly hope someone teaches this restaurant as well as others to take heed to the history of izakaya style dining. Go to Japan and learn from them since that is how they have always dined. Value wise, it was on the high end but that was to be expected. I would not have minded the price if the experience were better. I was so looking forward to this restaurant because my mother used to watch Emeril's cooking show all the time. Maybe my expectations were too high? I really do not think so. I would definitely recommend that you visit the restaurant but make it clear how you want your dishes to come out unless you do not mind eating everything at one time, which I do not.

text: The adventures of Katherine in insurance-land :( Well, the bf got his glasses here and they look and fit so good on him. And, I actually sat in on his exam and the optometrist was very thorough. And when I was looking at frames with him, I noticed the prices on the frames include actually the frame and lens and yada-yada coating in the price, and they are still very economical but also stylish. But, when it comes to my experience... yikes. I was recently in the store looking at frames and asked if they accepted my insurance - the manager said yes. Great, so, I actually called some other places were in-network and priced the eye and contact exam I needed. So, I finally called them last after all the other places, and got quoted 59 and 29 for eye exam and contact exam, which is a great price. So, I called another place that was on the way home from work, and figured that the price they told me was the best and since I love their frames, it would be best all around. Well, I call back to once again make sure the person told me right, got quoted the same price, but then heard the guy say something about 'out of network'. So, i told him, wait, whoa, the manager said you guys take my insurance. He says, we actually don't but we discount our prices for people with my insurance, then he says, on top of that, they discount 30%. Well, that sounds amazing, so I made an appointment. I go in for my appointment, fill out my paperwork, and once again ask to make sure about the pricing. Get a COMPLETELY different answer. They verified they don't accept my insurance, but say the exams are going to cost over $100. So, being me, I brought both the pieces of paper where I wrote don't the price quotes I got, showed it to them, they had no idea why anyone would tell me those prices. So, I'm not in the mood for haggling, I've come in for an eye appointment, and the attendant is really trying to work it out for me, but is still insistent that the price for the exams are $69 and $39, and there is no 30% discount. So, they go ask the dr. is she can adjust her prices. I'm feeling totally embarrassed at this point, I just want the services for the price I was quoted, TWICE. Apparently someone there has bad info and is spreading it around. So, they say I can just pay for what I can now, and pay the rest later, and they will honor the $59 and $29 I got quoted. At this point, I just want to get the exam over, it's getting ridiculous. I go in with the dr., she's annoyed, and takes my glasses to read them. The manager comes in again, and starts talking to me, which is a little annoying, because I don't have my glasses on and can barely see. She says, we'll just do the eye exam and I can come back for the contact exam. I'm just over it at this point, I say, nevermind, get my glasses back and just walk out. text: We ate here for lunch and their $25 three course preset menu is definitely worth the price. The salad was made with fresh butter lettuce and the fried strips of pig egg was a perfect balance with the salad. The soft boiled egg added more texture. The oysters were quite good. The gumbo was very light, not like your typical gumbo and it wasn't overly salted. The pork belly dish was a bit heavy and I didn't finish it because I was already pretty full from the appetizers. I'm not going to talk too much about the scrambled eggs. Nothing really that special here, that's what my fiance ordered. She just said "perfectly salted eggs." The dessert of course was amazing. The beignets were super light and fluffy. There were very airy and to top it off, the dipping sauces added to the experience. Service was very quick and attentive so no problems there. We sat outside which was very nice. If you can get out door seating I highly recommend it. Overal best 3 course lunch I've had in a long time especially for the price. This was also probably the least heavy of all the meals we had in NOLA. Definitely a must try if you're in the neighborhood!

Again, english is a second language to most of the staff but that doesn't bother me at all. The "head lady" was really friendly in terms of even helping me pick colors for my nails since I didn't really have a set color in mind, but I had a pattern in mind. After my eyebrows, I saw for my pedicure, midway through another lady started on my nails (efficient) and I also enjoyed my foot massage. I got the gel nails and it was done very well. Better than the other places I've been to. While my nails dried, I received a lovely shoulder massage...really nice. Overall, I felt I like I got a mini spa treatment. I would recommend this place. They take credit card but tips must be cash.
label: POS

text: Dean Team has done it again.. Super "caring carsalesman" up front who wants to put you in that 'perfect car for you' all the while using misleading statements and shady dealings to take advantage of you. DO NOT GO TO DEAN TEAM KIRKWOOD! Our car salesman Eddie/Edin showed us several cars that were in my range but didn't quite fit my needs. He dangles a 2011 Hyandai Sonata in front of me and tells me about all the perks, carefree maintence, free oil changes and extended warranties and in my price range! I took the bait hook line and sinker. The financing process was filled with calls to various banks, price variations on the car and already agreed upon price and mutitude of other frustrations. I inquired about paper work on the warranty and oil changes our salesman had repeatedly brought up to reassure me of what a safe and smart buy this car was to the finance manager. He tells me to check with Edi on that. As paperwork is finalizing ( finally! 3.5 hours after I test drove the Sonata) I inquire about the covered oil changes and warranty info and he tells me he will take care of it, get it in the system and have it with paperwork I was to pick up the following Monday. No paperwork involving what was included and covered was in my paperwork. I did not press the issue or give it much thought assuming that these upstanding honest folks at Dean Team wouldn't mislead me. We took our car in for its first oil change and guess what? No record of the included oil changes or maintence package. Nothing. When the actual salesmen was questioned about it he denied ever speaking of it and tells us that they don't even offer that! Of course they don't. I didn't just imagine the lenghthy conversation we had about cost of raising teenagers and how nice to have one less expense ( oil changes/ basic car maintence) with this particular car. It was spoke of more than once and I inquired to the finance mgr who didn't say "We don't offer that so lets clarify the matter with your salesman". He said Edi would have the information on that and to check with him. These guys are slick and they use manipulative tools of false reassurement to tell you what you want to hear to sign on the dotted line. Clearly I'm not alone in being screwed over by these shady salesmen. I only wish I'd read up about the dealership more before I walked in there. BEWARE in dealing with the guys at the Kirkwood Dean Team.
label: NEG

text: Have to give them a 2 rating for the position they put me in. I had taken my car there a few times and so I was fairly pleased with their service, I never felt pressured and felt like they were genuine people. My Volvo was driving strange, sputtering almost, and I DROVE it into the shop one morning before work. Come to find out they wanted to charge me $400 + dollars to change plugs, coils etc. Well my friend said he would do the work for cheaper so I denied the work. When I went to pick up my car, it would not start. Not only would it not start, the battery was almost dead and there was no manager on duty, only a clerk. He offered me no assistance until I asked him to call the manager regarding this. The Manager claimed that they drove the car into the spot it was in and that they didn't know why it wouldn't start. He offered me no assistance and no explanation, even though I drove the car into his shop and it was running when I brought it to him. I ended up having to tow the car on my own dollar back to my house where I found that my battery was now dead and that a series of hoses and tubes were not connected under the hood. I called the Manager again a few days after and explained that they did not leave my car the way I brought it to them (hoses, tubes, dead battery etc etc) and he did nothing other than blame it on his mechanic. This may have been a one time thing, but they left me stranded and offered no assistance when things were clearly wrong on their end. And to top it off, they charged me $60 for an engine diagnostic too. Choose wisely when it comes to these things...

text: I REALLY enjoyed this place. From the outside I was a little skeptical because of how dark it looks inside and the building is so old. But once I got inside I was made to feel right at home. The restaurant is family owned and they say it's their goal to make you feel like their having you over to their house for dinner. They accomplish this very well. Large portions with few choices and you can't go wrong with whatever you order. Excellent steaks and prime rib, great fish, soups and salads. One interesting dish is there baked potatoes. They refuse to tell you how they perfect the outsides but i figures it out. They take off the skin and then fry the baked potato so the outside skin is really good and unique. Last thing. DESSERT. the pies are amazing. The only problem Is that you'll be so full from dinner that you might have to get them to go. Overall, great food and classic dining experience

text: Food is excellent, one star off for service, ambiance. We had the jerk chicken, curry chicken, and oxtail. The tastes were exquisite. The jerk chicken and oxtail had a similar base- probably molasses underpinnings, with different surface spicing. The meat was tender without being dry. The rice and peas was also excellent and the cabbage fine- although on the sweet side. One reviewer mentioned bland. This was not my experience. Spicy means well spiced, not hot. If you want hot, ask for that. The portions are large. A small satisfies most, a large leaves plenty of left overs. The drop in star is for two reasons. The ambiance in the place is pretty bare bones. Not an environment in which you feel like hanging out. The other ding is that they screwed up my take out order. Ordered three things, they only had two wrapped up. I only live a 100 yards away, so walking back for the third was only a mild hassle. But a hassle, nonetheless. The guy at the counter seemed confused about the whole interaction.
label: POS

text: I took my guys here after work yesterday. It was Monday night football and we got there at about 7pm. Loads of space in here and we were able to sit in the bar near a tv. Some people started with the Guinness milkshake which they said was good but had very little Guinness in it. All the drinks here are pretty weak but nice. I had the blackberry mojito. It was weak but tasted good. TGI Fridays isn't the cheapest place and I think for after work drinks people want to taste some alcohol. We shared some starters. The jack Daniels sampler and green bean fries, buffalo chicken and loaded potatoes. It was good. It was all hot and we ordered another round of the chicken. The waiter was kind of odd. Maybe he was just nervous but he really didn't strike me as shy. Sometimes he just hung around the table when there was nothing for him to do. It was sort of awkward but also pretty funny. At one point someone asked him if he needed anything and he said "I'm just earwigging" strange dude!! I'd probably go back but it wouldn't be my first choice.

text: A brand new cupcake oriented bakery in an area that is sorely lacking in quality pastries. They specialize in gourmet cupcakes. The variety is quite nice, and the choices blew me away. Everything from pound cake cupcakes to a "pancake breakfast" cupcake with maple frosting and topped with bacon. I've been here a few times since it has opened and try something new every time. So far, I haven't found anything I haven't liked. On the down side, the place could definitely use some interior design work. While clean, the place is very, very plain looking and not that inviting. Even though it's a fairly small space, it looks empty. Some variety in pastries would also be a plus. the cupcakes are fantastic, but some times you're in the mood for a high quality donut or other pastry, which is not easy to come by without driving 20-30 minutes. Overall, they're off to a fantastic start. Give them a shot and enjoy some of the great flavors these gals are baking.
label: POS

text: What can I say?? This may be a Belleville institution, but we won't be going back any time soon. I visited Andria's with my husband and two kids on a Friday evening, after hearing a lot of talk about how great the steaks are. We made reservations, but they were clearly not needed. When we arrived at 6 pm, there were only three other parties seated. We all had steaks, again after hearing how great they were. After we had our drinks and the boring salads, our dinners were served. I will say that the baked potato was probably THE biggest I've ever had and it was cooked perfectly. The same cannot be said for the steak. My ribeye was greasy, full of gristle, and rather tasteless. My husband's ribeye was charred on the outside and overcooked in the middle, although he ordered "medium". Our daughters shared a ribyeye and theirs was more like mine...full of gristle and fat. We left hungry and disappointed. I will say that the service was excellent, but the food is not worth a trip back. What a shame!

text: I have no idea why this place gets such high ratings. I have been to the old location and now the new one and nothing has changed. If you liked the old one then why are reading reviews on Yelp? Just go on back. The Good: The atmosphere is pretty good. The place is very clean; way better than ZoZo's. The views are excellent. The wait staff is attentive, if a little hard to understand (thick accents). The Bad: The food is mediocre to terrible. An Italian restaurant should be able to make good lasagna. This is a standard. Theirs tastes like a bowl of runny meat sauce and soggy pasta with some cheese on top. Most of the ravioli is "eh" or not great. Oh yeah, oil, oil, oil. Everything...EVERYTHING is thick with oil, so nothing tastes light, just oily. Look, restaurants need to be rated on food quality and theirs is OK to sub-par. The Ugly: It would be alright if the place was billed a little less extravagantly. It's just too pricey for what it is. I guess if you want to take your date out, and impress her with your pronunciation of Italian cuisine, then yeah. However, expect to pay for the privilege.

text: I rented a car from Avis for a business trip to Chicago. Fortuitously, the car I got had Illinois plates and came with the EZ Pass for tolls. Picking up the car was easy enough. I had to park the car in the garage, figure out how to get OUT of the garage on foot (seriously, it wasn't easy), walk around the block to Avis and then wait for nearly 15 minutes with only one customer in front of me. The employee walked out to the garage to inspect each car. Considering I had to park on the third floor, this wasn't a quick task. He also had no sense of urgency when it came to the paperwork. My fiance was waiting outside to take me back home, so it was especially irritating as we both had to get to work. Honestly, it would have been quicker and easier to just drop the car off at the airport and take a cab home!

text: This food is practically crack! I wouldn't be surprised to find someone blowing the chef for the Slow Cooked Rabbit Leg & Dumplings out back of this place. I'm in from out of town and went with a couple locals, we all shared each others' food bistro style (recommend) in order to try more dishes. If you get the Molasses Cornbread, you will not be sorry. Grits were the bomb. My entree was "Trois Mignons," it was good and prepared well, but I would recommend trying out other entrees. As I hinted at the rabbit was off the chain. Also we had the Arugula and Heirloom Beet Salad, which was crisp and well balanced. Service was great. You SHOULD NOT leave this restaurant without getting at least one of the mixed drinks. They infuse their own liquors here. I can't remember the name of the drink, but I tried one with Cucumber infused Gin and it was the most baller gin drink I have ever had. It was very refreshing and the simple idea of infusing cucumber with gin is pure genius. Pimms cup was also good.

Rather than offering a solution to the problem, he stated "well, just to let you know by giving you the room (that we paid for), ill be kicking one of our employees on the street. Im doing this for you, just to let you know.". Maybe its just me, but I was shocked to hear something like this. We are two physicians who flew across the country to take our 8 hour board exam, and the last thing we wanted was a hassel, which ia why we booked this hotel. The room service staff was great, and the room was average but clean But its amazing how initial front desk service can make a huge impression on our stay. text: Ah. May. Zing. We could not have asked for a better team. We were fortunate in that we got to try the goods first, because our friends hired JAS Productions for their wedding, which happened during the time we were busy planning ours. Justin and Karen did such a great job that we immediately fell in love and were ready to hire them (let's not even talk about the other DJ companies we met with and what a joke they were...). Throughout the planning process they were both extremely personable, easy to get a hold of and constantly on top of things. All the planning forms and music requests list were online, which made everything super easy. As the day of coordinator, Karen made excellent suggestions for things we were grappling with, and even for things we hadn't even thought of. She was a great asset to have and I can't imagine having planned the wedding without her ideas and help! Our wedding day literally went perfectly, thanks to them. Karen ensured that the timeline was followed, and was very communicative with my husband and I about checking in and making sure we were ready for the special dances, toasts, cake cutting, bouquet toss, etc. It was nice not having to think about what to do next, relax and just enjoy the day and night! As the DJ, Justin managed to keep the dance-floor filled with literally everyone (our youngest guest was 2 and oldest was 91). He played lots of different genres, keeping everyone happy. He also didn't play the songs on our 'do not play' list, even though we had a few friends beg him to (Uhh, Miley Cyrus? I don't think so!). His mixing was excellent and I couldn't have been happier with his song choices. He also made some good suggestions for songs to use for the mother-son dance and garter removal. JAS Productions also provided us with up-lighting on the trees, which really completed the look we were going for--they were even able to match the colors to our themes. Overall, I cannot offer a single (constructive) criticism to the duo. Our day was perfect and it couldn't have been done without Karen and Justin!

text: I have been to a lot of international airports around the world. Some of those are mega size full of restaurants and fancy shopping centers. Ironically, what I remembered the most is walking or running long distance to my gate or just lost my way! Honestly, all I need at an airport is a cup of good coffee and my flight leave on time. What Tampa International Airport offers just as it, a user friendly facility for travelers. Well organized design starts from you entering airport driveway. Red and Blue sign boards separate various airlines to avoid congestions. Ticket counters have plenty self-check-in facilities and helpful staffs on site assist to get your luggages going. Good restaurants and hotels locate on the premises. Parking also well marked and easy accessed. Monorail locates on 5th floor connects you from long or short term parking area to airline terminals. Terminal entrances are divided before you get through security. Full body scanning machine replaced tradition pat down at security check point and only take 3 seconds. After that, you are in your terminal and your gate is just few steps away and you have plenty time grab a coffee or sandwich. The only thing I think the Airport can improve is their art displays. The place is slightly grey and plain, does not match our beautiful sunshine state images! Besides that, it is an awesome airport to start your journey!

text: Let me Preface this review by saying all of this was conveyed to the corporate manager who was at the restaurant.(you would think the place would run better with corporate there!!!) After a horrible experience at the Hash House in the Imperial Palace in Vegas, my wife and I decided to try the restaurant in Reno. We has heard some good things and figured that our first experience in Vegas may have been due to the fact that the IP is a dump. Well the Reno store was even worse. The hostess was fine and was the highlight of the meal. I ordered a bloody mary that tasted like tomato juice and vodka(unacceptable for a 10 dollar drink). After using every condiment on the table to spice it up I finally asked the server for a side of horseradish. Instead she whisked my drink away and 10 minutes later it returned very spicy. Usually thats perfect for me but something was off... turns out the bartender didn't have horseradish behind the bar?! so she spiced it with siracha!!!! Then our food comes and my food (chicken and waffles)is overpriced but okay,my wife's plate comes (fried chicken benedict) and it is served on cold mashed potatoes!! The decor is retro-tasteful, with cherry lamps, stools with shapely women legs, cocktail menus on vinyl and a blown-up piece of Edmonton skyline out on the back wall (but with other famous structures across the world strategically inserted here and there). The music the DJ plays is fun, danceable, and familiar. This is a place where you take your closest friends, have a drink (or fifteen), dance where you stand, and HAVE FUN. And when you're ready to have even more fun, you go to the back, try to fit into the photo booth and see if you can bottle the night up in that little strip of awesome. It's pretty cool. Second big plus - selection of cocktails. $12 each, but worth every single buck. They taste marvelous (and are quite strong)! They also have these zodiac shots at ridiculously low prices (I think it came down to $2 per shot) - those taste pretty great too! When we went here last September long weekend, they didn't serve food yet, but I hear that's coming soon (if it hasn't already). I think that could only be a welcome addition to the so-far limited but respectable menu. I personally have no complaints on the palate end of things. Third big plus - no cover, older crowd. Definitely a breath of fresh air after the usual stifling selection of clubs and bars in the city (with overpriced covers or a typically younger clientele). I've never been to the GoGo Lounge location in Montreal myself, but I've heard good things. If this is what this little gem strives to be, then I'm all for it! So to sum up, it's an intimate lounge - great atmosphere, weird retro but tasteful decor, good music, great cocktail selection, no cover, older crowd. And photo booth. Oh yeah, and very interesting washrooms. Now if only we could get one in Calgary...

The door is to the right of the main window and leads down a long alleyway into a courtyard. The entrance to the main dining area and bar is to the left (kinda do a u-turn). Bathrooms are cute, clean and separate from the main dining area - next to the outdoor seating in the back. Menu is interesting, drinks were solid and service was friendly and knowledgeable. The Good: -Raw Brussels sprout salad: AWESOME. Loved it so much, I tried to recreate it at home -Crispy pork shoulder: delicious and tender. Really well seasoned -Moscow Mules and Dark &Stormy: well-made drinks The Not-So-Bad: -Chicken liver crostini : good, but expensive for what you get. Not worth it IMO The bad: That they don't have a location in TX!

text: Clean open dining room with tables for 2 and 4 through out. Nice decor. Very nice display of the cupcakes. There are also electrical plugs only the wall, table high for your laptops, etc. Nice staff. COFFEE: I just had a regular brewed coffee. Very good, smooth. Did not need to add cream or sugar. CUPCAKES: I bought 1/2 a dozen to take home and 1 extra to eat with my coffee. Great cupcakes. It's all about the icing. The cake part is fine, but really not something you'd really enjoy eating without the icing. BUT, that is good in this instance. The icings & fillings are amazing! They are not stingy either, so with that pile of sweetness on top, you really don't want a dense sweet cake also. The "plainness" of the cake part worked perfectly to tone down the delicious sweetness of the toppings.

text: We tried something different for brunch, and holy clams, are we glad we did. We went to the bistro (Upstairs). Not only is the decor very nice, this place serves up a righteous pizza, delicious sliders, and the servers were all amazingly friendly. We had the pizza with bacon & goat cheese, which was the perfect size for two people. Crispy crust (but with enough give to make it chewy, too), and the perfect blend of goat and mozzarella cheeses, caramelized onions, and bacon. The sliders were amazing - just the right size (3 or 4 bites, depending on who's eating), and the Kobe beef was delicious, the crab cake was light and crispy, and the buffalo chicken was also very good - honestly, I didn't really want to share. They also do what looks like a pretty great all-you-can-eat brunch deal, too. It looked like a variety of pizzas and calzones, some bacon-laced mac and cheese, some garlic knots, two different kinds of salads, 3 different dressings, the tomato bisque, and some kind of chicken in a sundried tomato sauce. The server told me it was $10. Bonus: pretty much anything with bread (the slider buns and the pizza crusts, anyway) can be made Gluten-free. SCORE. Two hours later, we're sitting here going, "Holy God, that was great pizza." Guess who's coming back?

text: As a guy that has traveled from coast-to-coast I have eaten at burger joints from most everywhere in the continental USA. I live on the gulf coast of Florida now. 5 Guys burgers are good. Their fries are good as well. My 2 Star rating is for VALUE. 5 Guys is seriously Over Priced. For fellow traveler's that visit the left coast In-N-Out Burger is arguably better in flavor for both burger and fries and, they have "secret" combo's which you find out about after you've been there a few times or, if you listen to the regulars carefully while in line and you're the curious type you can get the order taker to explain these to you. Adds a bit of mystery and fun to the experience. You can get two meals for about the price of one 5 Guys and this is in California where the cost of doing business is much higher than here in FL. Another thing which sets In-N-Out apart is that they cater to peoples preferences and needs. Example: Gluten-Free burgers are available at In-N-Out. They'll wrap them in Boston Lettuce leaves for you. Just ask. They also have very tasty milk shakes. If you had a McDonald's, Burger King across the street competition between 5 Guys and In-N-Out the lines would quickly disappear from 5 Guys. Guaranteed. I'll say this for 5 Guys they load you up on the fries so, if you have a large appetite for fries you'll really like this about 5 Guys. On the other hand, if you're allergic to peanuts or don't like peanut flavored fries, not a big selling point.

text: Their kitchen cannot handle large parties, nor their customers with a party of 5 who are seated right after a party of 14. Our drinks, complimentary bread and appetizer were brought out relatively quickly, however, despite our 8pm arrival, our dinner was not brought to the table until 9:45. We were dining with our 5, 8 and 10 year old daughters, whom, by the time the food **finally** came out, were too tired to eat anything. The whole experience was terrible, the least they could have done was comp our appetizer, or maybe my boyfriend and I's 2 glasses of wine, but not only did they not offer that, they offered no real apologies either, simply stating that there was a big table ahead of us and that was just how it worked. I wrote a note on my receipt explaining to the waitress why I left her only a 10% tip (I am a constant 20% tipper, more if the experience is awesome) but I felt like she only did half her job. She needed to be the liaison between us and the management and make sure we left the table happy. I made it very clear that we were unhappy, asked her numerous times when the food would be coming out. She didn't even offer to bring more bread, or offer up another appetizer while we waited. If I could give it 1.5 stars, I would, but only because the food was good. They brought this awesome bread to the table with a sundried tomato and olive oil dipping sauce, very good amuse bouche. We started out with the Grilled Halloumi. This was presented as 4 filets of cheese grilled, served with pickle spears over some lettuce with balsamic dressing. I would give this dish a 4/5...very good. For an entree, I had the Beef Mousaka. This was very good, 5/5. I also tried my companion's Eggplant Karniyarik, very good also...4.5/5. Bottom line, get your food to go.

text: Alright, fair's fair, I almost never write reviews (especially ones this glowing) when I've only been to a place once, but when I came home and read the reviews, I felt this place needed a little more love. The situation: suddenly realizing I was a hairy beast, and my semi-regular wax spot's disorganized, overbooked, often-cancelled schedule was just not going to cut it (I'm sorry, Honeydew). The solution: Critical decision. Do I go to Emma or Anthony for a patchy cheapie job, or do I try something new? I called the next closest place. I was offered an appointment that evening by a very sweet receptionist. The experience: I showed up 20min early and was taken back right away to meet my waxer. Irina was the same lady who answered the phone. She was polite, friendly, and professional. Some places make you contort this way and that, but she did all the small adjustments herself, kept up conversation to distract me from the pain, and didn't make me get on all fours to finish the Brazilian (tmi?). Considering it had been a while since my last wax, there was minimal pain--way less than I anticipated, seriously. I think she uses the Gigi Honee wax, which is very gentle. Tweezers to finish off any strays were in antiseptic solution, and the supplies were all very clean. The result: For $35 (first time at the spa) I got a very fast, very comfortable (for a wax), very professional, very friendly Brazilian. Irina listened to what I wanted, did just that, and made me feel totally comfortable. How awesome is that? I can't vouch for other services, or for other people, but I am so, so very much coming back here. I'll update if my experience ever changes, but I have a hunch that I'm going to be going steady with Body Klinic. And judging by other reviews, I might totally be trying a facial, too.

text: In 1994, The Buffet was voted by the Tucson Weekly as the Best College Bar.... over 15 years later, I'd say it's Tucson's Best Dive Bar. The walls are covered in writing (the kind that you usually only find in the bathroom stalls of bars) and crowd is a mix of T-locs and college students alike. The drinks here are cheap, but there are only 3 beers on tap- Coors, Coors Light, and 1554- however if those don't float your boat, you'll just have to resort to a mixed drink. And if for some reason, you're not in the mood to drink- you can always get yourself a hotdog and play some shuffle board!

text: There are two important requisites for having a good time at Chima Brazilian Steakhouse: you need to love meat and you need to come hungry. The $50 charge per person is more than fair if you meet these requirements, but I definitely wouldn't bring some "first date only ordering salad" girl to Chima. The salad bar was great, but try to avoid filling your plate, as you will soon be inundated with a delicious variety of meats. Everything I tried was fantastic. The pork ribs were some of the best I've ever had, the lamb was amazing, and I could eat those little bacon wrapped filets all day. Service was nearly flawless, though they did forget is was my birthday, but they more than made up for that tiny mistake with an order of flan on the house. Not just any flan, mind you, but probably the best flan I've ever tasted. Chima is not a restaurant I would frequent, as I could easily gain 100lbs in a year if I ate there 1-2 times per week, but for special occasions or a particularly hungry party, it's hard to beat. We will definitely be going back, once we've had about a month to work off the calories we ingested. Thanks for a great birthday dinner!

text: Wow. I don't know what the heck happened to High Street Grill. Maybe they were off last night, maybe the owners went on their August vacation, but left the place open and run by teenagers, but I don't know. We got there, secured spots at the bar, and my wife had to use the restroom before she sat down. She walked away, and the bartender, who I've never seen before, came over to ask if we wanted menus. I told him yes, and that I wasn't sure what my wife wanted to drink, but I knew what I wanted. He walked away, and didn't come back. My wife returned from the restroom, and we started looking at the menu...once we knew what we wanted, we closed our menus, as is tradition, and expected the tender to come over and take our orders. He didn't. We waited. Finally, after about five minutes with no alcohol, he finally came over and took our order. I ordered a Belvedere martini, the wife ordered a glass of chardonnay. Her glass was fine...mine was a fairly small martini, something that I'd expect to get a diner, and it ended up being $11. Anyway, we their chips and dip for an appy, which are freshly cooked tortilla chips, served with fresh guac and pico de gallo. I tried to order the lamb burger, which they were out of, and were out of the last two times we've been there, so I ordered the smoked pork loin sandwich. My wife ordered a grilled chicken sandwich with pesto. It took nearly 45 minutes for our appetizer to come out, during which time we'd finished our first round, and had to wait 15 minutes to order a second round. Once the chips came out, they were delicious, as usual. Unfortunately, we then had to wait another half hour for our meals to come out. We were debating whether or not to get up and leave once the food finally arrived. My pork sandwich was phenomenal. I mean, just great. I'd order that again in a second, and cut you if you got near it. My wife's pesto chicken sandwich? Not so much. The chicken was very thinly pounded, and probably the driest chicken I'd ever tasted. It was smothered in mayo, with lettuce and tomato on top, and get this - HAD NO PESTO ON IT! I wasn't in the mood to argue with anyone, so we just dropped our debit card as soon as the food came out, ate as quickly as we could, and got the hell out of there. Honestly, after this experience, and the experience of a friend of ours a couple weeks ago, I'll think twice about High Street. Maybe John will turn it around, but I won't be going back for some time.

text: Soooooooooooooo thankful we found this place. It was our last night in NOLA and our plans changed because Essence Fest pretty much took over the Quarter. So, we stayed in the Garden District and walked to Magazine St, not too far from our hotel. Our goal during our trip was to search out all of the authentic New Orleans cuisine we could. When we got to Magazine St we couldn't find any place that screamed NOLA! Oh no! What were we to do?! After consulting our trusty Yelp apps, we walked past several spots and finally chose Salu -- what a great surprise! While not a NOLA-inspired menu, the menu here was vast with a smart variety of food for all palates. Because our livers weren't damaged enough yet, we ordered a couple of rounds of mojitos and caipirinhas (you know that Brazilian drink that tastes like tequila?). The classic drinks were only $5 each. Hellllooooo! I'll take one or two or three of those! Besides a good and inexpensive drink menu and GREAT food, we experienced some of the best service (though service all over NOLA was exceptional, for the most part). Our server was conversational and gave us suggestions on other really good restaurants for our next trip. In fact, she made a list and gave it to us. She also told us which bars she recommended in the area that were in walking distance from our Garden District hotel since we wanted to steer clear of the French Quarter. We felt like we made a local friend here. Thank you for good food, good drinks, and good conversation!

text: Tennou is definitely the BEST sushi place on the west bank! I've been coming here for years and am still satisfied with the food as the recession plays out. My boyfriend and I always get the beef tataki bc it is the best we ever tried. They give a generous portion compared to other sushi places and cut it thin the way it should be. It's also seared to the right temperature and the ponzu sauce goes well with it. Other places usually cook it too much and it usually is very bland elsewhere. And I LOVE the onions that go with it. My favorite rolls are the tennou II roll and salmon naruto. The sexiest man alive roll and hawaiian roll are pretty good also. My favorite salad is the tennou special salad (no whitefish and add avocado and cucumber!) Dessert-wise, the tempera cheesecake is THE BEST here. I've tried many other places like sake, rock n sake, etc. and its just not as good. The mango sorbet and red bean ice cream are also very good here! Service is usually good. The only downfall is that they sometimes charge for unnecessary things. For example, the charged me $1.00 to take out whitefish from the tennou special salad which is ridiculous! Other than that, I still love tennou over other sushi places on the westbank!

text: Since I'm off work for 2 weeks, I decided that it was the perfect time to try some of the newer places opening up around the Webster/Kirkwood area. On my list were Pickelman's, Fuzzy's Tacos, La Cantina, and Pazzo's Pizza. My boyfriend's best friend is in town for the weekend, and they are having a guy's night tonight, so he and I decided to go to lunch instead. I let him pick out of those four places, and he picked Pickelman's because he thought it would be the fastest. Boy was he wrong. We walked in and the line was so long it was comical. Wait like 45 minutes for a sandwich? I think not. So we went next door to Pazzo's, which was anything but crowded. Still, we stood there waiting for about 5 minutes to be acknowledged and seated, and then another 10 or so minutes to order. My boyfriend grumbled "This place is WAY understaffed," and boy was he right. There was ONE WAITER waiting on the entire restaurant, outside tables and all! That is just crazy. There is no way that you're going to get top notch service with one person waiting on the entire restaurant, no matter how good of a waiter/waitress he/she is. I ordered their lunch special, which is a half pizza and a half salad for 9 dollars. I chose the Del Pietro salad, a basic italian salad, and the Funghi pizza, with mushrooms, mozzarella cheese, and truffle oil, plus I added caramelized onions. My boyfriend ordered the Sugo's pizza, which had basically every meat that you can imagine on it (pepperoni, sausage, bacon, hamburger). My salad came out fairly quickly, and while it was strangely made up of mostly romaine hearts, the dressing was delicious, and I enjoyed it. Our pizzas were out in a reasonable time as well, but when mine arrived, I noticed that while it had almost no cheese on it, and was quite burned, it was missing caramelized onions. Before even taking a bite, I brought this to the waiter's attention (it took a while to flag him down), and he took it back to have them add the onions. For the first time ever, I had meat pizza envy, because the boyfriend's looked WAY tastier than mine. My pizza came back, with onions added, and I ate a piece, waiting for the truffle oil taste. OMG...they seriously forgot the truffle oil too. At this point, I'm just ready to leave. I sat there for about 10 minutes, staring at this pizza with mushrooms resembling canned mushrooms...very far from the tasty, wild variety...with no cheese, and no truffle oil, which was one of the 2 advertised ingredients. Finally the waiter came back, probably noticing that I wasn't touching my pizza, and I told him the issue. He agreed that truffle oil is very noticeable, and offered to take the pizza off the bill, or make me something else. My boyfriend said to get something else, so I ordered the margherita pizza to go, because he was now out of time and had to get back to work. I don't feel like the situation was handled poorly (the waiter was apologetic and very nice), but it could've been handled much better. One, they should've comped my food, because I sat there the whole time staring at my boyfriend eat, which didn't make for a very pleasant experience. Still, we ended up paying 30 dollars for lunch, and the margherita pizza was just ok, and not something I would get again. Two, if they were going to charge me for the remade pizza, they could've given me a whole instead of a tiny little half. That would've been the classy thing to do. And three, the only other person besides our one waiter there was a lady that appeared to more like management, and she never said anything to us about all of the mistakes, even though it was clear that for almost the entire time, I had no food in front of me and was pretty frustrated. I'd like to say that I'll give them another shot. It's close to us, we eat pizza A LOT, and we're always looking for new places to add to the rotation. Also, my boyfriend liked his, and I can see where there might be potential for me to like mine too. However, this experience was so bad that I'm just not sure I can be that forgiving.
label: NEG

It's an impossibility that any one place will serve the best of everything of a genre, but this place is the best "combo" I've found to date of: food quality, consistency, prices, decor, service and menu. Ironically, I have a few friends who absolutely hate this place and rant about the service. I think this is probably due to them coming during the lunch or dinner rush. I avoid that and generally go early or late and have a wonderful time, but it does seem like they're understaffed to handle a full house like is rapidly becoming common during lunch time -- so I guess the word is out about how good this place is. Virtually everything on the menu is consistently good. I don't think I've ever had a bad meal here. Their grilled pork spring rolls are huge and packed with flavor; their noodle bowls are standard fare; their Pho is well above average -- not necessarily the best Pho broth in the city (I'd say at this point Frosty's has better broth, but I'd rather eat in the more comfortable environment of Pho Orchid than be cramped into that tiny place overrun by school kids ordering slushies. Their lemongrass beef is excellent; their steamed rice vermicelli is awesome.. the Vietnamese poboys are one of the best food deals in the city... It is a Mexican tapas bar which I have never come across before, and it is such a welcome change to the typically large American/Mexican portions. We ordered 4 Tapas and an appetizer and we were blown away by each and every one. What we ordered: Japanese Oysters - WOW! Small, delicate oysters with a wonderful chimi churri inspired cocktail sauce Shrimp and Crab Empanadas - I am not usually a seafood lover but these empanadas blew my mind Chicken Tastatidos - The cutest little bite size tostadas with the most savory spicy marinated chicken I have ever had Cheese Tamale - Made in house and steamed to order - it literally melted in my mouth Short Rib Corn Cakes - By far the best dish of the night! The most tender, juicy short rib on home-made corn cakes, it doesn't get better than this. Cocktails: My boyfriend got a tequila flight while I consumed a house margarita which was authentic and simple. They do not make blended or flavored margaritas which I really respect. When I wanted to switch it up, I ordered the Stoli, blackberry and basil drink and it is one of the best drinks I have ever tried in my life (and I like to drink). text: Seems my poor car must have a "Hit Me" sign taped to it somewhere..... Don't get me wrong, though - I took this person's insurance info down anyway. I don't like being lied to, so I was prepared to call the insurance company faster than you can say "no turn on red" at the first sign of shadiness! To get the ball rolling, I wanted to get an estimate of the damage ASAP, so I went to a shop that I trusted with some other repairs, but they informed me that they couldn't help me with this issue and recommended Orsini's. I'm wary of new shops - we all know that some people will take advantage when at all possible. These guys were definitely NOT the type to do that. I walked in with no appointment and asked about getting an estimate - the secretary was very helpful and listened to my story, and put my info into the system immediately. After only a few minutes, Dan came over to help me out with the estimate - he talked me through what he found, explained the charges, and even talked me through how I should handle dealing with the people that hit me. He was kind, helpful, and not pushy in any way! He even emailed the quote to the other person when their fax number wouldn't work. A few days later, I received a phone call from Dan just to check in and see how things were progressing. Now that things have been settled (they decided to go through the insurance...woohoo!), I will be heading back to Orsini's for the repairs. They were fantastic at making a crappy situation a little less crappy. I have definitely never felt as at ease in a shop, and I consider that a big thing! All in all, the one thing that I am thankful for, out of this whole thing, is that I found Orsini's....though I hope, after this repair, I won't have to visit them again for a while!

text: Okay, so this place is essentially a mainstay in Rittenhouse square. I almost feel like I don't need to review La Colombe, as everyone is aware of its existence. So I have this complex opinion about La Colombe, but I think I've kind of seen the light for what it is. First off, yes it's inexpensive relatively for okay coffee. But you're trading off the fact that you're not getting great coffee. The coffee itself is nothing to write home about. I'd go without it. The espresso is good, I usually get a double macchiato or a cappuccino when I go there. I'd say that the place is fairly mechanical, and it will give you the same thing on a consistent basis. Speaking of consistency, you will always find yourself with a long line and seating is at a premium. You'll find a lot of couples who will be ravenous in the line, send one person to get a seat, while the other waits in line. This is the name of the game, as no one is really respectful enough to wait in line together. There's a tendency for there to be loud children with their parents, thrashing their strollers back and forth, trying to, simultaneously, annoy the shit out of you by making an obstacle course, quiet their crying child via carelessly rocking the baby without any regard to the actual problem, and keep talking about that new Dior bag that Veronica just could not live without that they just think is trite. There's a tendency for haughty privileged middle-aged couple to boast about their 401k's loudly in front of you in hope of you hearing how successful their meaningless life is. If you can't tell, I don't really like the fanbase that La Colombe has. Let me put it this way: I'm surprised I haven't seen Mary Kate Olsen talking about her Vera Wang snuggie in this joint. I've never gotten through an hour at La Colombe without the need of rolling my eyes at some absurdity like this. I'm always amused that these people that are enthralled by expensive things go to a place where the coffee is mediocre, and could be better somewhere else by just adding a couple of quarters to the price. I think La Colombe has a certain reputation of being amazing in Philly. I don't understand it though. It's almost mechanical, where people expect the same cup every day when they go here, and they will get it here. The blend never changes, from what I can tell, and there's nothing truly exciting about La Colombe. I like their carbonated water machine and almond croissant. That's about as excited as I get about this place. In summary: If you're a douchebag that's spent all but two of their dollars on a new Michael Kors bag, and you need to go to a place to be around like minded douchebags to display your newly acquired display of "wealth," get a coffee here, and put a bunch of sugar substitute and skim milk in it. text: For some reason, this restaurant reminds me of 'The Cheesecake Factory'. I mean, the menu reads the same, I think some of the dishes are similar and hell, both sell a crazy variety of cheesecake. I just wanted to point that out because I've felt that way for years. Odd similarities. Anyway, I've dined in this place SEVERAL times since 2005, when I first came here with my ex. Each time, there was always something weird going, either inside the restaurant or just outside the door. More on that later. This last time, I came in with some friends from Pensacola. Why on Earth they decided to dine at a chain restaurant for their first visit to New Orleans is beyond me. Have you ever wondered what the deal is with that? New Orleans is unique right down to the core, from the eclectic mix of individuals to the cuisine to the architecture. Why travel hundreds and sometimes, thousands of miles to eat at a chain restaurant that you can experience anywhere. Why not actually try something that's bred in the city you're visiting and remains only local. Does McDonald's in Atlanta taste any better than McDonald's in Texas? No, because it's friggin' McDonald's. In any case, this is what they wanted and so we decided to dine. As usual, while the hostess seated us immediately and was courteous, it took quite a while before we got a waiter. 10 minutes must have passed before we flagged someone down to find our server. Eventually some guy stumbled from the bar area to take our order. At first, we only ordered drinks and mine was a simple Jack Daniels and Coke. That's typically my weapon of choice, for those who don't know me well yet. The drinks took a VERY long time to arrive. Finally, they showed up and my friend's wife got the wrong wine. The waiter argued with us, explaining that we were wrong. The wine wasn't even the proper color. He finally went to the back and brought out what she had ordered. For the sake of keeping this review within the 5,000 character limit, I am only reviewing MY order. I placed a request for the Lemon Garlic Chicken with Rosemary Glaze and it came with garlic mashed potatoes. The food arrived promptly this time so no complaints there. My chicken, however, was EXTREMELY salty. I was surprised that the intense amount of salt content didn't dry out the bird. I then sampled the mashed potatoes and they, too, were overly salty. It took me almost 4 Jack & Cokes to rinse away the sodium. I also want to add that in all the times I have been frequenting this establishment, my entrees have either been too salty or too bland. Wait staff are not very attentive at all, especially when it gets later in the evening and there's usually a raucous going on inside or outside the joint. Allow me to explain.... The last three times that I've dined at this location, the police have been there and it's never on pleasant terms. On this last visit, my party and I walked up the sidewalk and two cop cars were parked nose-to-nose in front of the doors. When we walked in, our eyes immediately started burning and our noses running. It was from a cloud of pepper spray in the area. What the hell was going on?? I immediately ran to the restroom, where 3 women were seated on the bench just outside. Two of them were arguing very loudly and suddenly, they began exchanging blows. It appeared as if they had already had an altercation once earlier that evening. One of the women's dresses was ripped at the shoulder, exposing her bra. The other girl was laying face down on the bench. Another girl had a badly bruised eye and was covering it with a pack of ice. Another woman had scratches on her face and down her arm, clothes ripped. As soon as the two women began throwing punches, two cops rushed in immediately and grabbed the women. Someone fired off another round of pepper spray but I could not tell where it originated from. After I cleaned up in the bathroom and came back out, one of the women was missing and the others were in handcuffs. I saw what I presumed to be the manager near the entrance speaking to police, his hair disheveled and shirt wrinkled and un-tucked. Later, our waiter explained that the women engaged in a boxing match inside the restaurant when one of them was caught dining with the other's boyfriend. Punches were exchanged, the manager jumped into the fray, customers fled and the cops were called. Again, I'm just reiterating what the waiter told us. This is not the only time I've dined here where cops were called in. I'm going to close with this: The food is okay. That's all. There are better places to dine, in my opinion, especially if you're in the Uptown area. This restaurant is too streaky, suffers from poor wait staff, under-seasoned or over-seasoned dishes and seems to be a prime location for physical altercations. I'd pass on this one and you should, too!

text: We had a surprisingly good time at Bistro St. Tropez - I had not been for a few years and vaguely remembered it being decent but not especially memorable. We trudged our way through the design center, merrily window shopping along the way and arrived on the top floor where this restaurant is located. The wait staff went in a few directions - most of them were very efficient, quietly removing plates and refilling water in a formal manner, keeping their eyes downcast as if someone in the kitchen was waiting to hit them with a giant baguette if they dared to look a customer in the eye. Our main waitress Emma was a delight- charming and funny and she really added to our enjoyment of the meal. The décor seems to go in a few directions as well - part of the dining room is on the formal side with upholstered chairs, another section has fun, modish red chairs and various colored spot lights - I guess trying to create the South of France look. Another area has barstools up against a shelf that look out to the city and hubby mentioned it might be nice to sit there and have a drink and I agreed. There is a great view from the restaurant, maybe not the best angle to view the city from but it's nice to look out at all the sparklling lights. We went for the "Degustation Menu" of three courses for $28 which included a Starter, Main Course and Dessert. I started with a glass of Provencal rosé and was happy to discover it actually tasted like the rosés commonly served in Provence - dry and earthy with flecks of sunshine in it. Hubbies chilled cucumber melon soup had a surprising but delicious tomato base and was a sort of tasty gourmet gazpacho with chunky veggies. My roasted corn soup was very nice- smooth and creamy with a little sweetness from the apple and just a hint of smoke. A basket of fresh rolls with an enjoyable pesto/olive oil dip was served with the soup. Our entrees were mostly excellent - his scallops were perfectly cooked, sweet and nicely seared and he loved the eggplant "caviar" served along with it. Though I couldn't taste the "pistachio goat cheese crust" that was described on the menu my salmon and asparagus wrapped in phyllo was juicy and rich and very good. The ratatouille served with it was excellent; the grayish cauliflower puree was not since it was rather unappetizing, both visually and gustatorily (is that a word??). I choose the profiteroles for dessert and hubby had the praline mousse with a roasted peach. The choux pastry puffs filled with vanilla ice cream and drizzled with a thick chocolate sauce were good but honestly I like the way I make them better, these were a bit dry (whereas the ones I make are buttery and tender - no doubt mine are the incorrect way though!). His dessert was brought out with a smoking lavender frond to flavor the peach and it did that splendidly - the mousse was rich and wonderful. Between the wait staff, the décor etc I just had the sense that the restaurant has a bit of an identity crisis - is it formal or fun? Paris or the Mediterranean coast in summer? Their menu and service comes across as "Fine Dining" yet they have a wine club (buy 10 bottles, get one free) on their website - hmmm, I don't know. I do know we had a great night out - the three course menu was a good value and liquor was reasonable as well. It was nice to eat lovely food while looking out to the city lights.

text: This place is trying way too hard to be an exclusive "hip" spot. How people are raving and giving it 5 stars is a mystery to me... unless they somehow fell for the illusion that they were "special" enough to be let in to this exclusive establishment. I went with two attractive women, and upon arrival we rang the buzzer at the unmarked and un-numbered door and were greeted by a man we later learned was the owner. He looked us up and down as we asked, "Is this the Laundromat?" "No, there's a laundromat down the street." "We mean the bar Laundromat." "There's a bar down the street." "But we're looking for the speakeasy." A look of annoyance, then "Well what's the name?" "Hop Sing Laundromat." Finally we are acknowledged and told that yes this is the place (no numbers or signs because it is oh-so hip to do it that way). Once more we're looked over, this time staring at our feet. I'm told that my shoes are not acceptable (apparently no athletic shoes regardless of the rest of your attire). I mention we had walked miles that day & leather shoes weren't an option. "Go around the corner to the Chinese thrift shop and buy some canvas shoes, those are ok." So my $90 lace-up shoes are not acceptable but a $6 pair of kung-fu slippers are? Seriously? But my friends want to go in so I grudgingly comply and buy a pair. We come back with my ridiculous new footwear ring the bell, are now greeted by a doorman who doesn't even look at our eyes, but rather stares at our shoes as he steps out, and are finally shown in (and yes, we had to sit through the same rehearsed schpiel about 'you'll be disappointed and we have a tiny selection, oh wait, I have that backwards...' that everyone else wrote about.) As we're seated at the bar, I notice that it is so dark I can't make out anyone's feet, much less their shoes. Yes, the shoe rule is fucking retarded. So we sit at the bar, which the owner has said may have the largest selection of liquors in the world (and it really is an impressively huge bar with massive variety) and are handed a 2-sided drink list with 2 or 3 drinks per alcohol type on each side. Interesting choices, but I just ask for a vodka gimlet and am told sorry, we can only order from the menu. The incredibly limited menu. The owner just bragged about his huge selection, then we got to stare at it and not be able to order from it. Again, fucking retarded. Hell, calling that retarded is an insult to retarded people. The good parts: The bartenders were courteous, the drinks we wound up ordering were very well made and the price was reasonable at $10, and the decor was interesting. The bad: The level of pretension surrounding the whole thing was a turn-off. It really just felt like the kid who got picked on in school finally got to open his own secret club with his own secret rules... I'll show them! We just wanted a drink in a chill environment, not some elaborate footwear ordeal and Disney tour guide speech just to get to the bar, especially when the place only had 8 other people in it when we arrived.

text: This gym needs some more recent reviews, so here I am, to the rescue! This is the first gym I have ever joined. At Fitness Works, I was greeted warmly and simply by a friendly woman at the desk. I joined here about a week ago and have gone every day since. Everything is very clean and there are plenty of anti-bacterial wipes and paper towels to wipe things down before/after you sweat on them. Employees are friendly and informative. The front desk has some protein bar type stuff for sale as well as bottled water and other bottled drinks. They offer a nice variety of classes including spinning, Zumba, cross training, pilates, several types of yoga, and more. I haven't tried any classes yet, but I'm looking forward to trying a few of them. The busiest time I've seen so far seemed to be around 6-8pm (people are home from work, I guess.) But even then it wasn't so packed that I couldn't find a machine I wanted. 1-2pm was great, not crowded. Last night, I was finishing up around 9:30pm and was the only person left in the cardio area (they close at 10.) I love this place so far. It is more than what I need for a fantastic price. So glad it is a block and a half away from my house!

Our group was the table of 5. Each group had a different server, in case you try to blame the service I will describe on just being an overwhelmed Waiter with a 9 top. I was excited looking at the menu, and almost went for breakfast at lunch, but since it was my first visit, I played it safe with the burger, but opted to pay $2 extra for the sweet potato fries since I saw that they came with a side of creole tomato dressing. I asked if they came with some sort of sauce and Waiter offered to bring out some of the dressing. The bacon was left off of one co-worker's sandwich; this wasn't addressed with Waiter. Another coworker was served regular fries (kinda meh--seasoning reminded me of Rally's) instead of sweet potato fries. We each gave him a card, and when he brought them back, he set them all in a pile in a wet spot on the table, with a "Thanks, guys," and walked off. We were left to sift through the wet receipts and credit cards to figure out what belonged to who. I'd heard really good things about the food at this place, and would have been excited to go back and try the breakfast menu. text: We went there with another couple. We wanted to try a new steakhouse in New Orleans. I was excited to try this place because of the reviews on Yelp and their website made it sound really good. When we got there, they told us our table wasn't quite ready and directed us to the bar to wait. Well about 20-25 minutes later we were seated. We ordered drinks (which in my opinion were a bit over priced..$16 for a glass of wine that cost about $25 a bottle). Then we ordered our appetizers. After about 20 or so minutes or apps came out. The apps were really good. I had the carpacio, and the rest of the table had the crab bisque and the baked shrimp. All were very good. After our apps, we ordered the meal and thats were our experience went way downhill. I ordered the 14oz filet medium rare. The rest of the table had a NY Strip (medium), and two delmonico steaks( one medium rare and one medium well). For sides we got the "table" size sides. We ordered the onion rings, steak fries, creamed spinach, and asparagus. We waited for at least 30 minutes before the waiter brought us some bread. about 10 minutes after the bread we finally got our food. My steak, I have to say, was perfect and very very good. (should be for a $60 steak). The two medium well steaks were cooked medium rare. Neither person who got the delmonico steaks were impressed and my wife hardly touched hers. The strip was good but under cooked and went half eaten. Now to the sides. They were the worst side dishes I have ever had in my life. The creamed spinach tasted like eggnog. It had way too much cream and nutmeg in it. It was horrible. The onion rings were OK. The steak fries were actually the worst I have ever had. They would have been better getting their fries from McDonalds. The fries were actually a whole potato that was cut in fours length wise and then fried. They were flavor less, over cooked and so dry we could barely choke them down. The asparagus was grilled and charred but sort of edible. They didn't season them at all with oil or salt and pepper before grilling. The biggest thing about the appetizers was the size. We all ordered the "table" size apps and the size was laughable. The onion rings had about 6 rings. The spinach arrived in a small appetizer boat. The steak fries had 6 fries and we got about 6 asparagus spears. Each person at the table got one onion ring, one fry, one asparagus spear and a small dollop of spinach. There was one of each app left on the plate after everyone got one. I don't know who thinks this is a portion enough for a table of four but the portions of each app were barely enough for one. We were actually laughing about it at the table. We debated ordering the "table" size chocolate cake dessert for $25 but decided against it as we figured that the "table" size of the cake was probably just a standard sized piece that they would cut into slivers at the table. Other than my filet, almost everything else was either just OK to downright awful. I expected much more from a $350 meal. I was very disappointed with Chophouse and I will never go back there again. If you want an extremely good and always consistent steakhouse, just go to Dickie Brennan's.

All three of us ordered, but when it came time to pay, the woman at the counter forgot to include Sarah's order until I reminded her. This was an omen of things to come. It was like they had run out of their normal panini bread and had to make do with something else. But the most disappointing aspect was that Sarah had ordered a Veggie Quesadilla. text: Great potential, bad management. I had always enjoyed the atmosphere of this bar. Although the prices were always steep for both food and drink at this bar, the choice of beer tended to justify this premium. However, after years of patronizing the establishment, I encountered great frustration with staff wanting to serve people after 1:30 A.M. Due to the fact that they wanted to get home. This was on a Saturday night. After contacting the owner, it was clear that he blindly stands behind the poor customer service provided by his staff. After relaying my concerns of his staff ignoring a large group who came in during business hours (of which, two were drunk, and not drinking - not the rest!) in order to go home, I received this response: "I do certainly appreciate you relaying you concerns to me. Unfortunately it would seem that your entire group was intentionally given slow and absentee service do to what you feel was two "drunk" people in your group, but what my staff (with corroboration by video)felt was a majority of your group. One of the women with you fell not once but twice, two people at a table were having trouble staying awake and keeping their heads up. There was a conscious decision that your group had had enough to drink for the night, that the one round would be served and that was it. This was further reinforced with the aggressive and blatantly confrontational way which you approached Bruce the MOD. By ALL accounts (including a customer who has no vested interest or reason to lie) the way you approached the situation was the final deciding factor in refusing further service to you and your friends. In regards to your concern over the timing of last call, 1:45 is our standard and the standard across the city. Individuals ability to be flexible with that is generally exercised on slower week nights when there are fewer people in the bar and done to allow people that have been in the bar to have another drink while the bartender and staff start doing there cleaning. You would be hard pressed to find any place that will serve right up to 2, especially on a Saturday to a large group that spent most of their evening elsewhere. I am sorry if you disagree with the way my staff or I have handled this situation, but I do stand by their decision to stop service to your entire group based on the level of intoxication demonstrated by some of your friends. They did what they felt was necessary for the whole group and could not be expected in these circumstances to individually determine each person's sobriety level." This is in response to a letter to the owner stating that, after having my issue with their neglect of service, that I asked the manager for the owner's information, which was refused to me. I had to write down the owner's name from the business license on the wall. Although the food and drink is good, the occasional great server and bartender were greatly overshadowed by bad, lazy servers and bartenders, who apparently say they "flagged" a group of people because two were drunk. Devil's Den is incapable of serving alcohol, however will serve as a upper scale restaurant. Although I was never thrilled with the customer service before, I didn't think I would have to contact the owner, and then have the owner stand blindly behind his lazy Saturday night staff.

text: I am on the search for the perfect vegan cheesesteak. So often, I get a gourmet impostor that might be a delicious sandwich, but is in no way a cheesesteak. For shame. But Govinda's stepped up to the plate and played ball. I got a hot, messy chicken cheesesteak wrapped in foil, and it was excellent. I might've even moaned a little when I first took a bite. It wasn't trying to pretend it was healthy, and it was effectively comfort food. It was pretty large, too, and I was able to save half for dinner the next day. It held up! A caveat: both the chicken and the cheese are soy-based. They had good texture, and the cheese was surprisingly creamygooey*, so I'm not suggesting a total overhaul. Just maybe experiment in the kitchen with some seitan or nut cheese and see what happens. I don't get fussy about some soy here or there (it's certainly better than its animal counterparts), but diversity is awesome. And less likely to kill us. I loved the atmosphere of the take-out section, totally chill and not fancy at all. I could've been in any meat-serving joint in the city, and I wouldn't have noticed the difference, besides the menu. The service was great - pleasant, but genuine. The prices are more than fair, especially considering I made two meals out of one sandwich. I will definitely be back, I'll just make sure not to eat anything with soy for the preceding and following 24 hours. *no casein, though, in case you were wondering. They even say so on their menu, which is considerate of them.

text: I have eaten here several times and always get the vegetarian appetizer plate which I love. Recently though I ate here with friend and had the salmon. She asked if I wanted a box for my leftovers. I told her no as it was too dry to eat. She did apologize and then went and told the chef... Maurice. Maurice comes out of the kitchen, comes to our table to tell me that he heard I did not like the fish as it was too dry. Then he told me he had tasted the fish himself and "it was cooked perfectly" . Seriously, you come out of the kitchen to tell me, the customer, I'm wrong. And what are you doing eating my old food... that's gross. Why on earth would you do that? Simply rule here for all chefs and wait staff.... the customer is always right! Second, if you think that dry piece of fish is "perfectly cooked" you obviously don't know how to cook fish. I love the vegetarian dishes here... hummus, tzatiki, babaghanush, all delicious. And, yes, I will continue to go back for the veggie dishes. But the chef is an arrogant SOB (why else would he have his picture on his billboard?) who needs to rethink a few things. Why come out and tell the customer he is wrong? text: I started with the Morimoto Sashimi. The request to replace any shellfish with an alternative to accommodate an allergy was declined at it was against the chef's vision (forget about being against anaphylaxis, but hey), but the crab could at least be placed on another plate. For the price, you don't get a lot of fish (2 pieces of 4 fish and 1 crab), but they are incredibly fresh, which makes it worth the splurge. I picked Duck Duck Duck for my entree. The duck breast is amazing (the skin was fantastically crispy and tasty); the confit fried rice was delicious (I usually hate fried rice, but this is a different dish all together); and the runny duck egg was rich and soaked nicely into the rice. We finished with the Yuzu Meringue Tart, which was like a lemon meringue. The fresh mango provided a sweet balance, and overall the dessert was light enough that you should opt for it, even if you're stuffed full of other good food.

text: If you have the right look (lots of tattoos, shaved head or long hair, funky clothes, piercings galore- or top-notch suit and lots of cash) I'm sure you'll get the 10 star treatment. I give 10+ stars for quality and coolness, -9 for customer service. Us middle-class normal-type peons- seemed the expectation would be that we would kneel before them for even thinking of letting us in. You must be buzzed in- no casual walk-ins! I was wearing a Nate Nash shirt- maybe they assumed we had some money to burn despite being dorky suburbanites!! The place has this uber-biker/artist/hipster thing going. Though the saleswoman was a nicely dressed middle-aged lady at home in any snooty jewelry store, Evander and his buddies, sitting and chatting in the store, looked like they just rolled out of Easy Rider. Saleslady smirked at us continuously, esp. when my wife asked to see really cool rings, then saw the 15 grand price tags. Evander and Hells Angels gang ignored us completely. That said- this place is COOL. I say that begrudgingly, because really, what a bunch of snotty a-holes. But-- dude backs arrogance with real talent. Lots of hand-crafted jewelry and artwork, very top-notch (real diamond, 24-k gold, etc.) and unique, surely worth their price tag. He has hand-made beer, too. That was probably the only thing in our budget!! Be prepped to spend at least a grand for a nice tiny toe ring-- at least. IF they let you in.... PS-- The giant glass insects on the side of his building RULE. Got to give credit where it's due, even if I didn't like the service! (Note: This is same review I wrote as Preston Evander- Check-in had me check into the wrong name! This is correct business name.)
