All in all: I felt nickeled and dimed here, and I didn't feel like my feedback was valued when expressed to Matt. The negatives: Service. - We waited 10 minutes between receiving our menus and taking orders which, for a day time lunch service (and being the 2nd occupied table there), is a LONG wait. - We waited a good 20-30 mins for two wraps, a salad, three hamburgers and a roast pork sandwich. - After we were done, we waited ANOTHER ten to fifteen minutes to get our check. Did you catch the part about waiting? If we arrived when the place was full... thats one thing. We arrived well before the crowds and still waited, and waited, over forgettable food. When the place fills up, it's too noisy to carry a conversation. Summation: I can understand the appeal among the twenty-thirty something after work get-a-beer-and-pizza-and-watch-the-game crowd who doesn't care if they have to wait a long time. The beer list looked decent. But for a 'quick' lunch, or a work lunch, or a servicable dinner- I wouldn't return.

text: If you are ever fortunate enough to check out Virginia City, NV, you have GOT to try Cafe del Rio. Cute restaurant on the outskirts of Ghost Town, away from the hustle and bustle of the more touristy buildings. Yet, this building also has it's own history and period decorations of the old mining/gambling town Virginia City was at the turn of the century. We were fortunate enough to be the first guests of the evening so we had the whole place and the servers all to ourselves. We snacked on chips and salsa while looking over a very simple and defined menu. Our server said that everything on the menu was made from scratch. I though to myself, "Yeah right, they all say that," but I gave her the benefit of the doubt. I decided on the "Stacked;" a shredded beef (or chicken, or pork) dish baked between two corn tortillas, smothered in (I chose both) green chile and red chile sauce, and topped with a fried egg and melted cheese. DISCLAIMER: I am 100% Mexican and my mother makes a very similar dish that is fantastic. This dish was absolutely AMAZING!! The red sauce was as authentic as it gets; you could taste the freshness. I had no intention of eating everything, but I couldn't resist. It was THAT good! My wife had the fish tacos and those were delicious. My father-in-law had the Yucatan Enchiladas with shrimp and fish. That was great too! Even my kids' nachos were fantastic and very unique. This is my new favorite Mexican restaurant. Too bad it's so far away. Kudos to Cafe del Rio, Virginia City!

text: Have you ever purchased spices at Schnuck's or Dierberg's? Then you have wasted your money, sorry to say. The truth, however, is that if you want even the most basic spice and you want it on the cheap, Jay's is the place to go. If you want a giant stack of tortillas or pita (naan) for a couple of bucks, go to Jay's. If you want cumin, you can get twice the amount for half the price of local grocers. Don't get me started on the cost of Extra Virgin Olive Oil at the grocery story. Total rip. The truth is that if you want to flavor your food with anything whatsoever, you should go to Jay's. The quality is the same and often times better, the quantity is always more, and the price is always less. Beans. Rice. Soy Sauce. Garlic. It's all cheaper. Furthermore, if you look up a random recipe for some type of international cuisine that you have never tried before, Jay will have everything you could need and more. The first time I made an Indian curry, I gawked at the recipe because it called for like 15 different spices, none of which I had. I thought I would give Jay a try even though it looked kind of small from the outside. It had everything, everything, EVERYTHING that was on the list. ANDDDDD they have their own parking lot! As it turned out my mom and s-i-l were very happy with an asparagus salad they ordered. My brother ordered the lamb with grits...at least I THINK that's what the gummy salty mess was. The lamb was gamey and overall the salt was overwhelming. We were so horrified by the food my brother and I tasted each others. I ordered a special - a pork chop. The chop was super thick and a bit burned on the outside. But the real problem was how tough it was. I should have been provided a hack saw. The sweet potatoes...which I normally love...were so salty I couldn't eat them. The red eye gravy was bitter AND salty. What's up with all that salt? Why don't you let people salt their own food rather than be so heavy handed? I spent $200 on a meal I would give less than zero stars on if it were possible. Maybe other entrees are fabulous but I can only speak to what I experienced. My advice...go to Frenchmen's Street and try one of the eateries there.

text: I took a well worn pair of leather waterproof boots to Nick at Hakky Shoe Repair in Greenwood Mall. I asked that stitching be repaired and reinforced, that they be waterproofed and if the lining that had worn through be repaired if possible. Nick said that he could do all of that but that they may not be 100% waterproof but he said they would be waterproof enough to withstand dewy grass. I said ok and paid about $50. The stitching seems to be fine. If the shoes were waterproofed at all they did it without unlacing the boots and it was entirely ineffective. My first walk in dewy grass left me with thoroughly wet boots and feet. The large leather pieces stitched and glued inside the boots as the lining repair both had to be removed. The left boot was now to short and Dominic, Nick's father, ripped out the repair before I left the store. The right rubbed my ankle bone when I tried to wear them the first time and I removed the repair before leaving the house. I phoned and explained all of this to Dominic stating that I was unhappy that 2/3 of the $50 repair was not at all what was promised. He said he could do nothing but he'd ask Nick. Dominic called and offered a $10 refund. I told him I felt it wasn't enough but it was better then nothing. I live 30 min from Hakky so I ultimately asked in a letter that they mail me what they felt was an appropriate refund . It's been a month and I have yet to hear from Hakky. I purchased a pair of boots at the same time. I told Dominic that I wore a men's 8 wide perhaps even an extra wide. It's entirely my own fault that I didn't realize I'd been sold a 9 medium until I'd worn them outdoors. I went to sell them on eBay and discovered that the boots retailed for $80-$90 new. I'd paid $150. I feel that disparity is an unreasonable mark up. I regret not googling the price. Most of this exchange is my own fault. Nonetheless I feel that the ridiculous mark up and being given the wrong size in the first place speaks to the business practices of Hakky.

text: I took my jeep wrangler to get inspected and was told it needed $700 worth of work to pass inspection. My friend, who is also a mechanic but who does not do inspections, was willing to do the work for half the price, so I took the car elsewhere to get it fixed which Jeff at Just Cruisin' said was fine. I brought my car to my mechanic with the list of all the repairs that Just Cruisin' said were needed. While my friend was fixing my jeep, he noticed the left springs on both sides were completely broken through and was shocked that Just Cruisin' overlooked it. He did all the repairs and I brought the jeep back to Just Cruisin' for a re-inspection, again, as I was told I was allowed to do. After the second day, I still hadn't heard anything so I called and was told my jeep was all done but that they had needed to fix my horn and said I had to pay $25, which I said was ridiculous considering I knew my horn worked and they didn't call me first to authorize the repair. I picked the jeep up over the weekend and realized that they had left the key in the ignition (jeep has no top) and that they had not put the inspection sticker on, even though I was told the jeep was "all done". I went back as soon as they were open and was told that they deliberately did not put the sticker on because they knew I would not pay the $25 to fix the horn. I asked why they left the key in the ignition and they said they were too busy and did it by mistake (that would have been a great reason to give to my insurance company if the car was stolen) and I asked how they could nickel and dime me for $25 for an unauthorized repair but overlooked the broken leaf springs that could have caused the entire back end of the car to literally fall off to which they responded "we can't find everything". Joe was very, very rude and was very condescending and mean. Needless to say, I will never, ever bring my car back there again and will tell everyone I know about my experience because if nothing else, they overlooked a huge safety issue that could have killed me and my passengers if the broken leaf springs failed while I was driving it. Not to mention they didn't even apologize for the oversight and to top it off, they overcharged me for something that was not authorized. Heed this warning and take your car somewhere else!!!!!!

text: Oh Refinery, How I wish thee were five minutes to my house. I would visit weekly to try out the new items on the menu. Hard to really comment on what I ate because when someone reads the review, well it won't be on the menu to try it! But that is the beauty and the nature of this fine establishment as well as the torture. It's like a pop up kitchen every week in the same location. You have the most amazing dish and want to come back to have it again but instead, something even more amazing is in it's place. Fresh, seasonal, sustainable and knock-your-socks-off flavor profiles. Produce from local farms, the best goat cheese which is like a crack addiction, pork shanks and pbr mussells. I mean seriously... the menu reads like a Shakespearean sonnet for the 21st century hipster. I feel like we have an ouce of coolness and can hang with the bigger cities who have these types of establishments on every corner in San Fran or Eugene, Oregon. With the land of Tampa strip malls and the culinary collection of chain after chain, please take a moment and try this place out. It's not fancy, it's not pretentious, and it's not trying to be anything other than great. It accomplishes it on many levels. We get a bottle of wine, a couple apps, a main entree to share and a dessert to split and I think our bill was like $60 bux with tip. Where else can you dine so well on a pricepoint like that?? nom, nom, nom

text: This is one of my favorite running trails in STL. If you go from end to end, its about 16 miles. I've run this trail after work in the early evenings and it isn't too packed, and on weekends it generally starts getting busier around 9 a.m. There are lots of different people who use this trail from runners, walkers, bikers (who all usually announce as they are passing and don't try to mow you over like they do at other parks!) so it's always a nice mixture of people. Mom wanted the chicken pita wrap with extra tsziki sauce; I ordered the chicken pilaf bowl; and my fellow ordered the Friday night chicken dinner special (lemon chicken with potatoes and Greek salad) which was the hostess' suggestion; we were delighted to see that the stuffed grape leaves were also a Friday special, so of course we had to order them! $52 was the total tab, but we figured that we were getting a lot of food. We were told at around 8:15 that the food was almost ready to box up, so I suggested that my guy should go home and feed his cat before joining mom and I at my house. The food was not ready until almost 8:45. At some point the gal out front said that they had run short on the chicken and had to prepare more for our order. By the time I got home with the order (I live across town by the airport) it was about 9:20 and we were all famished. I heard my boyfriend groaning when he opened his cardboard container...looking over his shoulder, I saw 2 chicken LEGS and about a cup and a half of chopped potato pieces - THIS was his $16 chicken dinner special?? For what they charge, they should tell you straight up what pieces you get in this meal. My guy liked the taste of the chicken, but honestly, it was not enough food for him for dinner and he is not a big man. I opened my chicken pilaf bowl and couldn't find the feta cheese or the tsziki sauce that is supposed to come with it, nor could I find the extra tsziki sauce that cost $1.50 (my mom wanted that). The chicken wasn't so bad, but the rice was dreadful: sticky, over-cooked and over-powering in lemon flavor (almost too tart). This rice was also included with the grape leaves, which closely resembled meatballs (not the tender, rice and meat stuffed dolmades I've had elsewhere, like in Greece) They were not seasoned, greasy, and actually left imprints on the rice "bed" beneath, I would assume because they were so heavy. The only person who was satisfied was my mom, who said her pita was delicious. Of course, her feta and tsziki sauce weren't MIA, so I'm sure hers wasn't so bad. I will also make note that the grilled pita wedges we received were very good...but would have been better if we could have dipped them in some tszki sauce (the extra that we paid for and did not receive) I called the restaurant and spoke with the manager, who said he was sorry that the chicken dinner didn't meet our expectations and would pass it along to the owner. He also apologized about the missing items, but I had to ask if he would provide them if we came back over there (which we didn't, because our intention was to dine together at home and watch a movie). I don't like to speak poorly about any establishment, but after this experience, I truly felt like a victim of P.T. Barnum: a true sucker, and no, I will not give this place another chance.
label: NEG

text: Boo hoo, Mr. B's. I hope today's lunch experience was an anomaly to the wonderful times past. I'm bereft with disappointment. We pointed out that salmon is an unlikely resident of the Gulf, to which the waitress responded, "well maybe it's a fish that goes by several names, there are some like that." She later explained that "they just hadn't changed their menus, but that what it should read is fresh fish of the day." When it arrived, the salmon bore no resemblance to being fresh, was overcooked, and salted to death. Let's not concern ourselves with the mushy vegetables on the side. I do believe I've sampled better versions of this entree on overseas airline flights. When my coffee arrived at the end of the meal, the coffee cup had a sticky residue all over it, making it a most unpleasant encounter to the hands and lips. Beyond the mediocre food experience, the environment in Mr. B's was nothing like I've ever seen it. Yes, the dress code at the door states "casual." But it was disheartening to see men in flip flops wearing ball caps at the table. Possibly because I've only been to Mr. B's during weekday lunches, my perceptions are skewed toward the more professional environment--and possibly food prepared for regular customers with high expectations. They did have a decrepit but endearing musical trio, including a banjo-playing singer who brightened up the place thoroughly. Had I been there just to have a drink at the bar, watch the Saints' game on the television, and enjoy the musical trio, my report might be a great deal more chipper. But my mood is reflective of the lousy lunch on which I've just dropped $70 at a place that surely can do better.

text: TL;DR - Excellent location, great price, lovely courtyards, lackluster service, disappointing room. My family and I decided on this hotel above all the others in its price range almost solely because of the photos of adorably-decorated rooms full of charming antique reproductions and beautfiul secluded courtyards. When we arrived, we were greeted by less-than-enthusiastic staff. Different staff members we encountered on subsequent days were much more friendly. We were led through a winding maze of old buildings, which lent a "secret garden" feel to the whole affair that I absolutely loved. The layout really is very fun. The courtyards really are as adorable as pictured. They're shaded and breezy - a great place to sit and enjoy your morning coffee. As we walked past some of the rooms facing the courtyards, we noticed several broken shutters, which didn't give a very good impression. The rooms... not what I expected. We had selected standard rooms. Of course I didn't expect them to be as charming as the "deluxe" rooms (which are what you see in many of the room photos for this hotel), but I did expect them to be in good repair. We were given two adjoining rooms, and both rooms had charming French doors and great climate control, but the fun stops there. The room was a decent size, and it was clean enough, but it had way too much furniture. A pair of chairs, a large table and a floor lamp completely blocked the walkway to the adjoining room, so we ended up having to move our furniture in order to make it functional. When I attempted to sit on one of these chairs, I found that it was broken and would've probably fallen through if I'd put my full weight on it. The bed in my room was very uncomfortable - very saggy in the center. Walking around, it seemed like every floor surface (carpet and tile) was covered in a slippery Pledge-like sheen (Scotchgard maybe?) - if you're not careful, you can easily wipe out and land on your face. In the bathroom, the tub surround was cracked, our shower curtain was torn and hanging off several hooks, and our mirror was chipped around the edges. Furthermore, our room had no windows - we had two sets of French Doors, but one set had no shutters on its windows so it needed to be covered by heavy drapes. As a result, the room felt dark and gloomy. The adjoining room was better. They had a comfortable bed, a more spacious layout, chairs that weren't broken, and two large windows that made their room feel bright and cheerful. The first night we were there, I dipped my feet into the beautiful large pool near the main courtyard. I was impressed with it - it was an even nicer space than the photos suggested. The smaller pool was interesting, in a tiny courtyard, surrounded on two sides by low-hanging plants, but equally pretty and inviting. The following morning, however, I got a better look at those pools in the daylight and found them to be ABSOLUTELY FILTHY. What I thought was a dark-colored bottom was actually a light-blue bottom nearly completely covered in dark algae and dirt. They obviously take the time to skim off the debris - even the small pool that has trees hanging into it was clear of floating junk - and the filters were running, but they most certainly did not clean. They were disgusting - I can't stress this enough. I really regretted even dipping my feet into the water. It's an old building so I'm not deducting any points for this, but the rooms are not terribly quiet. Luckily, this place is in a great location (away from the chaos of Bourbon) but you will still hear people in the rooms above and near you, and there was definitely a lot of noise from the nearby staircase. It wasn't bothersome enough to disrupt sleep. Room service is apparently hit-or-miss. Our beds were always neatly made and towels and toiletries replaced, but the adjoining room didn't fare so well - they did not receive replacement washcloths or soap, so we had to share. Neither of the rooms received extra toiletpaper when that got dangerously low - we had to ask for more. The continental breakfast was actually pretty good - better than what you see at many hotels, at least - and the area of the lobby where it's served is quite nice. And it was great to have good coffee and hot tea available there 24/7. Overall, I can't say I'd choose to stay here again. The location is terrific, and the price is right, but there are so many other similar options in the area I can't help but assume that some of them must be at least a little better.

text: I recently purchased a blighted property with my siblings in Mid-City. We are historically renovating the property. We began plumbing the building and planned on replacing the existing water meter, which has not been updated since the house was originally built in 1910, with two new meters and new pipes that funnel to our water meters. I spoke to the House Connections department in SWBNO and she quoted the installation cost between $1,800 and $2,500. She explained that sometimes an installation can cost upwards of $5,000 for a meter installation, but we would only have to pay $2,500 at the most. I received the estimate ten days later: $5,068.20. This was only for one meter and we would have to pay the whole amount. When I tried to understand why it was so drastically different from the other prices I was given, they explained that it is never the SWBNO's policy to give clients average price estimates, even though two of her employees already had, and she referred me to master of maintenance. The master of maintenance had very little insight as to how the water meter installation prices were actually determined. He said this was the SWBNO's primary contractor's domain: Fleming Construction. He said Fleming Construction set the prices and SWBNO followed suit. He tried to help to the best of his ability, but the reality was that he merely managed SWBNO's contract with Fleming. I called Jefferson Parish's water board to see how much they charged for installing a one-inch water meter. They charge a flat rate of $1,500. The city pays for the pipes on public property and the homeowner pays for the portion within their property line. I discovered that most municipalities across America operate in the same fashion (Chicago, Illinois, Tucson, Arizona), and some counties go as far as incur all of the costs for new meter installation, because they regard it as standard updating and maintenance of infrastructure. Other city's water utilities provide thorough pricing schedules for different types of water meter installation scenarios. The pricing reasoning is well documented and fully accessible to the customer. This creates a predictable and fair planning environment. SWBNO's policy of expecting homeowners to foot the entire bill for maintenance and updates that should have already occurred stands in direct opposition to Mayor Landrieu and the City Council's goal of fighting blight, fixing the condition of our deteriorating streets, and minimizing city operating costs. Investors require a predictable and transparent city government. Most investors can absorb a certain amount of variable costs, but I doubt that after someone has purchased a home, and then secured a construction loan like we have, that they will be liquid enough to pay a little over $10,000 to partially subsidize a municipal service that should have been maintained. As a historic district, most of the Mid-City housing stock boasts water meters from when the neighborhood was initially drained in the 1910's. We later discovered that our existing meter was made of toxic lead. If we ever hope to address the chronic blight that has pre-dated 2005, then we must not penalize would-be investors by forcing them to pay for the mistakes of a mismanaged bureaucracy. We must fairly and efficiently address our infrastructure while also mending the structural issues of the SWBNO that have culminated in this citywide crisis. I am not an engineer, economist, or a city planner, but since no one in the SWBNO seems to hold these credentials either, I feel equally qualified in stating that updating the pipes in such a piece-meal fashion will ultimately waste time and money for the city and Orleans Parish taxpayers. In my subsequent dealings with the SWBNO I learned that it contracts out all of their engineering, maintenance, and pavement repairs to private contractors. The employees manning their offices have no immediate access to these contracts, making it impossible for home and business owners to coordinate reasonable time schedules for repairs and updates occurring on or near their properties. As the city considers another price increase for the SWBNO's services I believe we must seriously consider what services they actually provide. Much scrutiny has been directed towards the SWBNO's Director Marcia St. Martin's salary, pension plan, and performance as a director. They are well-deserved critiques and must not be abandoned. Further inspection should also be directed toward the employees of the SWBNO. There are undoubtedly many hardworking and experienced individuals at the SWBNO, but I believe those who are none of those things outnumber them by a great majority. The Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans is not just another utility company. It is charged with working against extraordinary subsidence, functioning as a stopgap against disease spurred on by standing water, and keeping our city from drowning when it rains. We have to expect better.
label: NEG

text: "Looks like I'm the fool again, I don't like it." - Tom Petty Tom was talking about love, but for me, I'm talking about a national chain that simply has not lived up to expectations. Mind you, some of this is my problem, and so this will be a cautionary tale for you. This story starts over two years ago when we are remodeling my home. Lumber Liquidators is having a sale that is very appealing, and they are providing a great deal on financing. The process begins, and, as I'm a novice with a sort of odd floor plan, I have them come out and measure my house prior to my purchase to ensure that I get the right amount. The young man arrives at the appointed time, measures, gives me details about all I need, and I show up at the store and buy what he told me to. I'm spending something like $8,000 for the product alone, on sale. I finance a huge chunk of the purchase and pay cash for the rest. As home, do it yourself remodels go, this project took a long time, and I only recently finished the floor. Now here is where it get's frustrating. I've got over $800 worth of extra, un-opened, factory quality, wood left over. This is beautiful stuff, I have no qualms with the quality of the product. Now, I know it's been two years, but I'm thinking that there is something the store can do for me. I was wrong. No help. They told me to post it on Craig's list and a builder might want to take it off my hands. Yea, that's a great plan. I tell the Assistant Manager on the phone to please brainstorm all possible options and give me a call the next day. That never happens either. So, I buy $8,000 worth of floor, I pay $100 to have somebody they recommend do the measuring, I buy what I was told to buy, I store it properly for two years, I install it well, and they will not take back or credit me for the extra unopened boxes of wood. You might be wondering, 'what does the purchase order allow?' This is a great question. I re-read the agreement, and, sure enough, that's what is written in the fine print. There is a brief period of time, 90 days or so, in which to return unopened and new products. This is the part that I need to own. What was I expecting? I guess I was expecting compassion, a buyback program, some sense that they understood what I was going through. In short, something more than I got. Is the product good? Yes, heck I think it's great. My only hope at this point is that you get to benefit from my frustration. Read the contract, install in a timely fashion, and don't expect a lot of compassion from the retail outfit. I might buy their product again, but it's hard to imagine right now.

text: I arrived in MSY at 2AM on a Thursday morning. I had not made a prior reservation with Aiport Shuttle, figuring if I could find someone at the airport who was also going to downtown New Orleans and wanted to split a cab, I'd rather do that and save some money and stress (having read the reviews here). Pluses: - Easy to find. Signs are visible as soon as you come out to baggage claim. - Friendly staff. Despite it being 2AM, the lady at the counter was super nice. - The driver was very nice and helpful - only 20 dlls one way. Minuses: - We sat in the shuttle at the airport for about 35 minutes, waiting for other passengers, before taking off. What you need to know: - They will assume you're purchasing a round-trip shuttle and will ask you when you depart. If you want a one-way ride, just let them know. The lady was very nice about it and said to call them if i ended up needed to book them for a ride back. - It is a ride-share, so expect to be driven around before being dropped off at your location. This will add to your drop-off time and it is an inevitable aspect of this type of service. - There was A LONG line of people waiting for a taxi at 2AM -- the 30-minute wait in the shuttle was actually shorter than the people who stood in line waiting for a taxi. - I didn't book a shuttle ride back from my hotel to MSY since my flight was departing MSY on a Friday afternoon. You can take a taxi to the corner of TULANE & LOYOLA -- the N.O. Public Library -- and from there catch the E2 bus to the airport (takes about 45 minutes to get there) and charges you 2 dlls. Monday - Friday, this should be okay since the bus runs regularly during the day. My cab from the French Quarter to Tulane & Loyola public library cost 7 dlls. Have exact change if you take the E2 bus (there's a walgreens across the street from the library, if you need to make change).

I've tried a number of their pasta dishes and absolutely loved the baked cannelloni and Rigatoni di Tocco. Both are rich and savory and consistently top of the line. Portions are large so if you have an appetizer or salad, be prepared to take home part of your entree. Their garlic cheese bread is phenomenal and the cannelloni bites appetizer are fried bits of goodness served with their amazing Italian gravy and a sprinkle of fresh shredded parmesano-reggiano. My husband loves their fried mushrooms, an easy app to fail on due to the need to cook them long enough so the insides are done but not so much that they are like chewing acorns. Salads are great, a mix of iceberg and spring greens and the Tocco special salad is a meal unto itself. House dressing is a balance of not too sharp and not too sweet Italian. The restaurant is definitely a smaller family affair but that appeals to me. I like feeling like I'm in my neighbor's home with family photos on the walls. Sure, the booths may have a spot or two of wear but to me that adds to the charm. I've seen reports of slow service in other reviews but never experienced that myself. I've had consistently good service, frequent check-ins by staff and even by Mama Tocco herself, who can usually be found in the family booth. This is definitely a favorite place for our family and an area gem!

text: Lolita is a nuevo mexican cantina located on 13th and Sansom right next door to Barbuzzo. This is an important piece of information, for otherwise you could walk up and down 13th and not locate this place. It is a small joint (seats less than 70) and has it's name written in light grey on the bottom panel of the glass wall. Even after you discover it, you would wonder if this is not an extension to Barbuzzo itself, and indeed on the sidewalk it's hard to tell where the outside seating of one restaurant ends and where the other's begins. Seems fortunate, or maybe it is by design, that the owners are the same for the two places. Whether there is some deep aesthetic reason behind this occult appearance, or it's merely a gimmick, Lolita succeeds in drawing throngs of customers. It doesn't take reservations by phone or the web, it doesn't accept credit cards although entrees are priced higher than $20, the servers are efficient but brusque; in other words, it does its part in trying to drive away the hordes, but it is oh-so-crowded. Especially on weekend nights. My friend asked how does the phenomenon occur, and frankly I was not 100% satisfied with the answer the Lolita experience provided. Lolita is a B.Y.O.T(equila) place, and so in the half an hour we were asked to wait before we could get our table, we popped into a liquor store and bought a bottle of 100% agave 'juice'. While checking out, the cashier took one look at us four people buying a single bottle and remarked, "Must be for Lolita!", stressing and lingering on the last syllable long enough to lend it a mischievous lilt. (For me, personally, that was the harbinger of the night ahead - but that's another story.) We eventually got into the restaurant, hungry and thirsty, and immediately ordered off a pitcher of the traditional lime margarita. Another quirky thing about this place is that all the food must be ordered at the same time. For a moment, I feared all the food will appear at the same time as well. Fortunately that was not the case. We ordered two vegetarian appetizers. The traditional guacamole was garnished with jicamas and served alongside three kinds of chips, the usual corn, plantain and colcassia (or arvi as we call it in India), and salsa both verde and traditional. The beet and mango salad was served with arugula and a plantain pakoda, dolloped with soft goat cheese. The guac was a little too salty, and the salad had nothing outstanding about it either. The margarita, on the other hand, was pretty fabulous. For entree, I went with the carne asada - medium-rare tenderloin served in a mash of creamy plantain on top of fried yuccas along side traditional salsa. The meat was succulent, and the dull taste of the plantain crema went well with it. The semi-crunchy yuccas also interspersed well with the sinewy meat. I tasted a bit from the other's as well: the salmon and the veggie enchilada seemed a bit mediocre compared to the beef, although the fried tofu in the latter was a treat. Summary: Lolita is a bit on the expensive side, and frankly I do not see why I would choose this place over El Vez which is right opposite it. The latter takes reservations, accepts credit cards, is much more expansive and has a better decor. Nonetheless, the food and margarita is decent, and I would recommend Lolita if you have been to El Vez before - at least twice.

The servers are for the most part super rushed, non-attentive, and some just have poor attitudes, as if their customers are burdens to them. Sitting outside seems like a really good idea for people watching/getting bumped into by everyone walking by, but you will wait twice as long to be served or paid attention to since your server can easily hide inside. I had to go inside and find mine once. The drinks, oh the drinks. I have been here many a time for drinks alone and I don't know why it took me so long to figure out that they are underwhelming and way over priced. They have what appears to be a decent selection of classic and craft cocktails, some of which are ok, but it appears that these bartenders have memorized the small list on the menu because when presented with the request to make something off menu (an old fashioned, mind you) the product is made incorrectly and you are charged $13 for it. I appreciate their absinthe selection, and their absinthe service, but that is about it. I am not sure why I keep coming back to this place. I guess it is location alone. It is a place I can take people from out of town with the pretense that "it is in a great location and is great for people watching, but don't expect too much."
label: NEG

text: It's a shame this place can't get it together, the food is good. A few weeks ago, I tried calling to place an order and the call went directly to voicemail. Specifically someone named Alex's voicemail. I found out via their facebook page they were having an issue with the gas company so the were not open. Craving their food at this point, I tried again this past Friday. I called the number on the menu 4 times (this number has also been programed in my phone for over a year), only to have it ring about 10 times and then go to Alex's voicemail. I checked their facebook page, and tried calling the number my phone directed me to via the facebook page. Success! Someone answered and it was the correct location. I attempted to order and was told I needed to call the other number. I told them that I had tried calling a few times and there was no answer. The conversation went like this: Circles: "did it go right to voicemail when you called that number?" Me: "no, it rang about 10 times and then went to voicemail" Circles: "well you must be calling the wrong number then" Me: "i know I called the correct number because I've been ordering from you for almost 2 years now" Circles: "well I can't take your order, this is for the restaurant only, you'll have to keep trying that number" I hung up the phone and threw away the menu. I should have stopped ordering from this place 6 months ago when a friend's credit card number was stolen after she used it there and she had her identity stolen. I know we're desperate for good Thai food in this town, but it's no excuse to make it virtually impossible to order delivery and/or have your identity stolen. Beware and don't think you've found your 'old reliable', they'll let you down.

text: Never again. We arrived for a quick dinner as we had purchased tickets to the nearby IMax theatre. We were seated by a hostess who expressed that she worked three jobs and about 90 hours a week. We then waited an eternally long time before the "server" arrived. We expressed our need to rush and ordered our drinks and burgers at the same time. The "server" took our order and then disappeared. From our vantage point, we could see the servers' station and the computer screen indicated we were the third of three tables that our "server" was working at the time. Of the three, one already had their food, the other was in the process of paying. We waited 18 minutes before our iced teas were finally brought to our table. The server apologized by stating that she had "been working another table and they were difficult." Clearly, she was unaware that we had watched her go behind the bar to respond to text messages instead of bringing us our drinks in a timely manner. After an additional 20 minutes, our burgers arrived and it was ashamed we had run out of time to enjoy them. We gobbled down our slightly overcooked entree's without our "server" ever checking on us or noticing our iced teas were empty. I left the table to get to the theatre in time to purchase popcorn while my dinner partner waited to pay the bill. He had to call our "server" over in order to get the check. The place has a nice atmosphere but service was, without exception (the food runner didn't even know what the dishes were that he was bringing to our table), pathetic.

text: So if you spin a tale about how you allegedly studied the fine art of bread making with some famous dude in Italy, does it make your pizza customers give you way more stars than your food/service actually deserve? Apparently. Every time I go in this place I expect Ashton Kutcher to jump from under my booth and scream "punked again!" From the "I know you ordered a veggie lovers pizza but my stoned assistant made you a meat lovers so eat it & smile, bitch" to the selling you a fountain soda and giving you a totally blank look when you ask for your money back because of the "broke" sign on said soda machine that they were clearly aware of when they sold you the soda. I sometimes wonder if Natty doesn't videotape the clustetfuck interactions with his customers just to have something to watch and laugh at when the shop closes. This place is consistently inconsistent folks. And proscuitto garlic knots does not a good pizza shop make. Sure the garlic knots are good but I've come here for PIZZA - not some lame excuse for using up the dough. Sure Natty is nice to share his life story with you but again - doesn't translate to delicious pizza in my pie hole by the end of said life story telling. THIS PIZZA SUCKS. I actually happen to be in the 1% of native St. Louis people who actually know what a New York style pizza is supposed to be. How is that, you ask? Because I worked at the long gone but not forgotten fabulous pizza place called Brooklyn Bridge Pizzeria during the 80s. The place where the owner, Steve, would crack your knuckles with the hot pizza paddle if the pizza u made wasn't perfect in every way. If that guy hadn't taken his pride & ego back to New York when he hit a snag with the health department Brooklyn Bridge Pizza would still be serving hundreds of slices & pies per day & the likes of Natty's & Racanellis would be laughed out of business with their lame attempts at New York pizza. New York pizza is supposed to have a crisp crust with a slight crunch to go with the chew. The crust should be able to hold the pizza up when you lift it to bite - not be a runny, drippy sloppy mess as is the case at Natty's. Most times the crust at Natty's is still doughy which tells me his oven temp & cooking time for the pizza is WAY off. Every time I have eaten here I have overheard at least one phone call from a delivery & one conversation in the restaurant about how they are dissatisfied with their pizza here. How does he stay in business? Because so many are willing to trade liking the pizza here for liking the quirky, eccentric owner here. I like him, too. The obvious embellishments in his life story tale make him interesting & endearing. They do not, however, make him a man who understands the fine art of New York style pizza making. BYOB - you betcha - you're going to need it to help you drown your disappointment when you realize this is just another crap pizza joint in a City already overcrowded with crap pizza joints.

text: I visited Saudia's July 21, 2012. I took a friend here because we wanted "Soul Food" and the person had already tried "another" establishment in the past. Now, I did call ahead to ask if there was a sitting area and was informed they have a couple tables - and thats exactly what they have. This location is not for you to take a friend to sit and eat and chat. I mean, that's what we did, because we were from out of town (NYC) but basically this place is best for take-out only. Now, on to the food. I must say, I investigated a bit before visiting, so I was looking forward to the Cuban Turkey Wings, but they we all out when I arrived. So I had the smothered turkey wings with mac & cheese and yams. The wings were very well seasoned and fall-off-the-bone tender. The gravy was alright, it could have used a bit more salt or seasoning. But you could tell the wings were marinated or something because the meat was seasoned all the way through. Yams were nice and sweet, even a little gooey - yum. And the mac & cheese....Let me say this. I LOVE cheese, and LOVE mac & cheese just as much, so I'm very critical. This mac & chesse was great. It was different, with some extra seasoning you don't typically find in southern mac & cheese; something with herbs because I saw the green specks. High levels of yumminess! I will caution you: if you are diabetic, you'd better stay away from that orange drink - you've been warned!!! Its very good, but VERY sweet. And the melted ice doesn't even dilute it so that should be a sign. Overall, the food was good. Like I said, this location is best for take out and I would have loved to try some other dishes but they were finished. Definitely a place to try out!
label: POS

text: I don't normally write reviews, but I really feel like something needs to be said about this jeweler. If I could rate them zero stars, I would. My fiancé purchased my engagement and wedding band from Hiller. At first he was very happy with the service when they helped him select and order the ring. The problem came when I needed to have the ring sized bc it was very very slightly too large. I went to have the ring sized smaller and when the ring was returned to me it was much much too tight and the prongs of the diamond setting were slightly tilted. (I have a four pronged diamond solitaire) when I went back to Hiller to explain it was much tighter than I expected it to be and it was now slightly crooked they charged me to size it again and told me there was nothing they could do about the now leaning setting. The girl at the store pointed out that no one would probably notice. The sizing wasn't an issue (although I don't like having to pay for something that should have been done correctly the first time) but how can you damage something very expensive and valuable to a person and then say there's nothing you can do and send you on your way? The work done was just sloppy. And the way they handled it was insensitive. I wish this is where my experience with them ended but unfortunately my fiancé also got my wedding band from there bc it was only way we could easily match the engagement ring. When the wedding band arrived it was first off sized differently than the engagement ring. It seems to be about a quarter size larger. As well the width of the band is larger on the wedding band and the engagement ring so that it does not match well at all. (the band is a very thin micro-pave setting) My fiancé and I now live and Houston (we had a surprise work transfer mid engagement) and are not able to come back to new Orleans until our wedding in two weeks. There's nothing we can do but either send the ring back and look elsewhere or have the ring sized here in Houston. I just want to make sure to let everyone else know about my horrible experience so you can avoid going through what we did. Getting your engagement and wedding bands should be one of the happiest experiences in your life. I now have a crooked engagement ring and a mismatched wedding band (that my fiancé paid a very large amount for!) Hiller's work is sloppy and their employees unprofessional. I would avoid them.

text: I'm updating my review since I had the unfortunate bad luck of ending up in the hospital last week. I had been having flu like symptoms and was diagnosed with stomach flu at the doctor. After a few days of meds, nothing changed and I still had a high (102) fever and adbominal pains. Called my doctor, who told me to go to the ER. And nine hours later.... I was admitted. Yep, NINE HOURS. It took that long to get in, get triaged, get a CT scan, and get seen by a doctor. Then get seen by the doctor again. Then wait for transport to my room. It was so ridiculous that the nurse told me, after I finally got put into a room, that I was next to be seen. It took forever. And then some. I'm sure there were sicker people there. But my doctor was outside my room almost the whole time. He wasn't rushing to see emergencies. I FINALLY got taken to my room. I had requested a private room because I was having some pretty nasty GI symptoms and needed my own bathroom and privacy. And of course, they rolled me up to a double - occupied- room. I lost it. It was 1:30am, I was feeling like shit, and I threw a toddler quality tantrum. No one cared. They pretty much forced me in the room. I had no choice. I was on the "waiting list" for a private room. I never got it, after FOUR DAYS of being in the hospital, every doctor treating me requesting it for me, asking every nurse I had, my dad calling the admitting department, talking to the floor coordinator more than once, and basically begging. Nope, I had to share a room, with no room for visitors or my stuff, people bumping into things any time they needed to get close to take my vitals, etc, and not being able to close the door of the bathroom (due to my IV lines) while I had diarrhea every 30 minutes while my roommate's several visitors were in the room. I am so pissed that I'm sharing that lovely fact with the Yelp world. That's how humiliating it was for me. I couldn't eat the entire time I was there, so I can't comment on the food this time. But the staff was really good, except the person my first night who didn't care that I was bawling my eyes out. But... the care does not make up for my excruciating time in the ER and my humiliation in not being able to get a private room. I don't think I can ever come back here. I don't like Barnes, but I'll try anything over MoBap after this experience.
label: NEG

text: I was afraid that my wedding dress hunt would be a nightmare. Not only is my wedding over a year away, but my fiance was coming along to help me choose my dress. Most salons aren't used to either....it seems to make them sort of skittish. Michelle at Swoon was completely a dream come true to work with. She was gracious and greeted my fiance and I warmly when we entered her store. Add one star. When I showed her a few pics of the type of look that I was going for and that I really wanted an American designed and manufactured gown, her mind went immediately to work. I don't know if Michelle has a categorical inventory of her stock of sample gowns in her head.....but it sure seems like it. Add another star. We began with a few lacy gowns, whose fitted waists couldn't get over either my chest or hips. I'm a big girl...but Michelle NEVER even remarked about it. Off she went to hunt down more gowns. One more star! After trying on four gowns....I found one that I liked, but wasn't in love with. Two more gowns later.....I'd found THE ONE! It was made in America, in my price range, in my favorite fabric, not strapless, had a train.....it was exactly what I wanted. My fiance was on the verge of tears! Add the veil that Michelle found that had that touch of lace that I loved....I came close to swooning right in front of the mirror! A person who runs a bridal boutique should be many things: Between the obvious pride Michelle takes in her shop, her product knowledge, and the impeccable customer service, she's got it all. Two more stars If you have the cash to spend, because the gowns that she carries are about $1500+ , this is the go-to place in the Reno-Tahoe area. I will purchase my gown and flower girl dress from Swoon and recommend the shop highly to all brides!

text: Many, many years ago when I was just a tourist and did not yet call New Orleans home, a good buddy of mine decided to take me and a crew of friends to Crazy Johnny's. It was one of the best meals I had ever had, and was the beginning of my romance with this part of the world. I am happy to report that well over a decade later, this place is as fantastic as I remember it. Completely void of any pretense and brimming over with simple, honest charm, it also serves up the best steaks around. Dickie Brennan's and Ruth's Chris are fine establishments but can't hold a candle to Crazy Johnny. And considering how inexpensive Crazy Johnny's prices are, it's no contest. Best damn fillet Mignon I may have ever had, and it was less than 17 bucks. Madness! The prime rib? It looks someone found a giant pink elephant, sliced it's ear off and served up on a plate that can barely hold it. Worthy of tipping over Fred Flinstone's car. And man, oh man it is so tender and delicious one does not need a knife. Afterwords, however you will feel compelled to fall into a meat coma. Resist this urge and order one of their special house coffees. Bliss. I will not wait so long to go back next time!

text: I've never felt happier or more comfortable in a hair salon. As a recent transplant to New Orleans, I was on the hunt for a good haircut. Spending the last four years in Philadelphia, I struggled to find a hair stylist who really gave me what I wanted. My last haircut was in January, and it took months of growing out for it to relax into something that was manageable for me. The weekend before last, I poured over Yelp reviews to try to find a place I could afford, and that had the right vibe. I had been recommended Paris Parker, but looking at the website, I decided it was a little too bougie and mainstream. I went onto Rocket Science's online appointment booker and Katherine had availability for later that day (I was pretty antsy to chop off the little mullet I had grown, due to this southern heat), so I took the plunge. Rocket Science was exactly what I was looking for. Perfect ambience... hip decor and rad-looking ladies on staff, with rockin' coifs of course. I spend enough time in the morning worrying about what outfit to wear that I can't be bothered to spend hours blow-drying and straightening, which makes my hair look too flat anyway. Somewhere between wavy and curly, my hair needs a very special kind of layer to sit right. Too often, I've had stylists give me cuts that needed to be blow-dried or straightened, despite telling me that it would be "wash and go." Katherine did exactly what I asked her to, and nothing more or less. Lots of choppy layers to accentuate the natural texture, recut my bangs, kept it long in the front and short in the back. She totally "got" what kind of hair of I have, my maintenance routine, and was totally respectful of that. She was a generally awesome human being, and I can't wait to go back!

text: Do you all remember that Star Trek episode where the main characters travelled to an alternate universe? Everything looked the same, but it was an evil mirror universe? Kirk and Spock in this alternate universe were bad guys and evil as opposed to good and benevolent as they normally are. Well, Winghouse is the alternate universe of Hooters. I walked in, and it looks and feels exactly like Hooters. The difference becomes apparent when you have to interact with the staff. Whereas the staff at Hooters are friendly and smile, the "Winghouse girls" seems to have an attitude and scowl at you. I suppose some people are into that sort of thing. The girl that greeted me at the door asked if I wanted a table. I said "No, I'll sit at the bar". She made a facial expression that expressed displeasure and walked away. I originally stopped in for dinner. Being alone, I sat at the bar. After sitting there for about 10 minutes a brunette named (I think) Krista stood in front of me not saying anything. So, I politely asked for a beer. She turned around and got it, and placed it in front of me, and walked away. (no words spoken.) A few minutes later I asked her "Do you have the ability to turn on the hockey game?" (I wasn't sure if they even got the correct channel, hence the question). She walked away, and I never got a response. Being that I didn't want to beg for her time so I could place a dinner order, I left the money for my beer and went elsewhere for dinner. Summary: If you are looking for a familiar setting similar to Hooters, but you want to be treated as if you are dining with Klingons, you'll probably enjoy Winghouse. Personally, I won't be going back.

text: Great ambiance! Great food! Live music on the weekends! I saw this place featured on the Food Network and decided to make a small day trip out here just to try out the tri-tip sandwiches. So, yeah, I guess I was being a touristy noob :P The drive and the scenery was absolutely breath taking, it was so lush and green, I almost wished there was a hiking trail nearby so I could enjoy the beautiful hills and the tiny little river that bubbled along. The restaurant itself made me feel claustrophobic, the food and the menu was just meh~ to me, nothing really to write home about. Solid fare: BBQ ribs, Beef sandwiches, Burgers, Chili etc. It was tasty, but not really outstanding. They seated us right next to the open fireplace with was nice b/c it was cold. The real treasure is outside though... They had live music, and a huge BBQ grilling station outside for their tri tip sandwiches. There is a little collection of random old miner era buildings in the back which is interesting, and a little house that someone wrote "I pooed"d here" on in huge red letters. We got the tri tip sandwiches, and listened to live music and mingled with bikers. It was definitely an experience and I would recommend this place to tourists... mainly b/c it's really a one of a kind experience. Where else can you experience an old miner town feel restaurant with an outdoor BBQ, with bikers and live music surrounded by stunning nature?
label: POS

text: DO YOU LIKE WARRANTY SCAMS AND HOSTILE TREATMENT? Then, by all means, visit this place. After being a loyal customer for years, and spending hundreds of dollars there, this is the treatment I recently received: I had a tire replaced under a road hazard warranty they sell. Instead of the replacement tire costing me about $50 (including mounting & balancing), it cost me over $100. When I asked why, I was told that the warranty company changed the terms. Interesting. I had 2 or 3 replaced there previously at around $50 each. After I reluctantly paid them and was about to drive away, I noticed that my key did not lock in place when fully extended, or fold fully into the remote housing when closed, as it did before I gave it to them. When I brought this to their attention, the owner was adamant and repeatedly asked me "How could we have possibly done this?" I told him that by twisting the key in the lock too hard, it would cause the two halves of the remote to separate and loosen the key. He completely denied that they could have possibly caused this problem, so I informed him that on a previous visit, they lost a center cap to one of my wheels when they inspected it. At this point he glared at me, and said as belligerently as possible "So you're saying we broke your key, and now you're accusing us of stealing from you?" To which I replied that my key was working properly before I gave it to them, and a center cap was missing from one of my wheels immediately after a previous visit. His response was "If these things keep happening to you whenever you bring your car here, that should tell you something." I was confused, so I said "Excuse me?" His reply: "Don't keep coming here!" Rather than continue to argue with him and waste my breath, I just left. It's really a shame that the owner, Jerry, is so ignorant and abusive. There were some really nice guys that worked there, like Dean and Craig. I pay $180 apiece for high performance tires for my car, but my dollars will go to someone who values me as a customer, and provides good customer service instead of abuse.

text: My husband and I decided on a Saturday night ( around 7 PM) to go out for mexican food on our way to an art event that started around 9:00. ( YES, I know.. text: Fare is easily in the top 3 new restaurants I've been to this year and I never saw it coming. It's nice to be surprised. Words like organic, local, and sustainable get thrown around a lot these days. Too frequently in a concern to be granola friendly, restaurants forget another important word: "delicious". Fare does amazing organic with aplomb (and without the dreadlocks). The space is well appointed and chic without being cold. Even better, their staff is invested in the concept - knowledgeable beyond the rote citation from most servers. We talked about everything from sourcing to flavor profiles to technique. Our wide tasting menu, recommended by Fare's gracious owners and staff, had plenty of highlights: - Farmhouse Flatbread - Get this immediately. Go now. Green Apple and Vermont Cheddar and House Bacon drizzled with Maple syrup. I could not stop. - Bison Sliders - Best Bison I've had east of Colorado, amazing herbal notes, lovingly seasoned and seared. - Gazpacho - Unbelievable nuance and depth. Sumptuous is not too strong a word - and we are talking about cold soup here. - Crab Cakes - Very solid, but not "Baltimore" Solid. Still better than most outside the Chesapeake - Grilled Octopus - Well balanced, not overpowered - allowing the meat to speak clearly. Perfectly fork tender. - Zuchini Fries - Paper thin, airy, deep fried. The real secret is the zing they get from powdered Red Wine Vinegar. Scintillating. Yknow what? Stop Reading. Go Now - Surprise yourself.
label: POS

text: I don't believe I've ever seen such a high concentration of cougars shaking their asses in one place as I did during my time at the French Market Festival this past weekend. Seriously. These women had it going on. My friends and I were completely threatened by their fuckme hip movements and sloshing wine glasses. If this is what being 60 looks like - consider me ready. In hopes of being comprehensive, there was more to this event than excellent live music and mad dance skills... What a whimsically beautiful event! The only thing missing was a stash of fireflies floating overhead. We arrived too late to enjoy many of the delectables I had originally planned to gorge myself with like beef beef bourguignon, cheese and pate platter, escargot, etc. Julia Child would have been impressed by the work of St.Joan of Arc volunteers. I ended up having the French Onion Soup (was hoping for something wilder, but all of the other options had ran out) and beignets (waited in line for 45 minutes. Worth it for three puffs of doughy powdered sugar goodness. It's not every day that Cafe du Monde rolls up to your back yard!). I really appreciate that French Market is free and open to all ages. It brings in a fun and eclectic crowd. For a moment of silence from the packed festival, we mosied our way into the church. Ahhhhh. Serenity now! If you want to feel in Europe for a moment while still being in the Circle City, I highly recommend slipping in to churches like St.Joan of Arc Cathedral. Lessons learned for next year's highly anticipated return visit: -Arrive early for food availability and to get a table (hot in demand). -Brush up on dance moves, so you don't look like a dork standing beside women old enough to be your grandma.
